item.title: APC chieftain to DSS: Scrutinise Dino Melaye’s statements
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi An All Progressives Congress (APC) chieftain and loyalist of President Bola Tinubu, Khamis Musa Darazo, has urged the Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies to scrutinise recent statements attributed to former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye, concerning the 2027 general elections. Darazo, who made the call while speaking with journalists in Bauchi on Thursday, said the move was necessary to safeguard national security and prevent political utterances capable of heightening tension or creating unnecessary apprehension among Nigerians. He, however, cautioned that his call should not be interpreted as an attempt to intimidate opposition politicians or suppress democratic freedoms, stressing that democracy accommodates criticism, disagreement and healthy political competition. According to him, political leaders must recognise the responsibility that comes with public statements, particularly as the country approaches another election cycle. “This is not about persecution, intimidation or silencing the opposition. It is about responsibility. If a statement made by a prominent political actor has generated legitimate security concerns, the authorities have every right to seek clarification and establish the facts,” he said. Darazo maintained that security agencies must apply the law fairly, irrespective of political affiliation, warning against the use of national security as a partisan instrument. He also urged Melaye and other political leaders to exercise restraint in their public statements, saying Nigeria could not afford another atmosphere of political tension, fear and confrontation ahead of the 2027 elections. “Political disagreement is normal in a democracy. What is unacceptable is allowing political competition to gradually become a source of tension among citizens. We should sell our ideas, present our records and persuade Nigerians rather than create unnecessary anxiety,” he added. The APC chieftain challenged opposition politicians to focus their campaigns on policies, programmes, leadership capacity and verifiable records rather than provocative statements capable of distracting attention from issues affecting Nigerians. He said supporters of President Tinubu were prepared for the 2027 political contest and would continue to defend the administration based on its policies, achievements and Renewed Hope Agenda. “We are not afraid of opposition. We welcome competition. But competition must be democratic, peaceful and issue-based. President Tinubu will be judged by Nigerians based on his record, just as every opposition politician will be judged by the people based on what they offer,” Darazo said. He called on the DSS and other relevant security institutions to remain professional, impartial and guided by the law in handling politically sensitive matters. item.title: 'He was going way too fast' - Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez escapes unhurt after smashing a £300,000 Ferrari
item.description: Robert Sanchez Chelsea 2025-26 - Getty Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez has escaped unhurt after crashing a £300,000 Ferrari into a barrier at around 70mph during a track day at the Nurburgring in Germany. The Spaniard, currently on loan at Como, lost control on the notorious Caracciola-Karussell corner, before climbing out of the wrecked car and helping to collect the debris strewn across the track. Sanchez loses control on infamous Nurburgring corner Sanchez was behind the wheel of a pink-camouflaged Ferrari 488 Challenge Evo when he lost control at around 2.30pm on Monday. According to The Sun, the 28-year-old was taking part in a public track day organised by Circuit Days, with six of his friends watching on. A British holidaymaker who was driving behind him in an Audi TT said: "He was going way too fast on the turn travelling up to 70mph. He slammed into the corner and the track immediately got red flagged. It's a banked corner that goes on more than 180 degrees and he clearly had put too much gas on and drove straight into the barrier." Sanchez walks away unhurt and helps clear the wreckage The front of the Ferrari was left in a crumpled mess, and the circuit was closed for about an hour while track staff repaired the barriers. The witness added: "The front of his Ferrari was completely demolished and parts were sprayed all over the track. Sanchez escaped unharmed. He came out the car immediately after like nothing had happened and starting picking up the broken pieces." Sanchez's friends also stopped to help gather the debris into bags, before the car was taken away on a recovery truck. Goalkeeper keeps his helmet on to stay incognito Sanchez seemed keen to avoid being recognised, with onlookers only realising who he was after spotting his name on the side of the car. The witness said: "He was wearing his normal clothes and a racing helmet. He didn't take his helmet off for some time. It was like he wanted to remain incognito, a bit like Stig. Even when the car got delivered back to the car park, he didn't want to take his helmet off for some reason." The Nurburgring, nicknamed 'The Green Hell' by Sir Jackie Stewart, was the scene of Niki Lauda's horrific crash in 1976. What's next for Sanchez at Como? The Spaniard will now hope to put the scare behind him and fight for a regular place, with Como facing Cagliari on November 21.
item.content:encoded: Robert Sanchez Chelsea 2025-26 - Getty Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez has escaped unhurt after crashing a £300,000 Ferrari into a barrier at around 70mph during a track day at the Nurburgring in Germany. The Spaniard, currently on loan at Como, lost control on the notorious Caracciola-Karussell corner, before climbing out of the wrecked car and helping to collect the debris strewn across the track. Sanchez loses control on infamous Nurburgring corner Sanchez was behind the wheel of a pink-camouflaged Ferrari 488 Challenge Evo when he lost control at around 2.30pm on Monday. According to The Sun, the 28-year-old was taking part in a public track day organised by Circuit Days, with six of his friends watching on. A British holidaymaker who was driving behind him in an Audi TT said: "He was going way too fast on the turn travelling up to 70mph. He slammed into the corner and the track immediately got red flagged. It's a banked corner that goes on more than 180 degrees and he clearly had put too much gas on and drove straight into the barrier." Sanchez walks away unhurt and helps clear the wreckage The front of the Ferrari was left in a crumpled mess, and the circuit was closed for about an hour while track staff repaired the barriers. The witness added: "The front of his Ferrari was completely demolished and parts were sprayed all over the track. Sanchez escaped unharmed. He came out the car immediately after like nothing had happened and starting picking up the broken pieces." Sanchez's friends also stopped to help gather the debris into bags, before the car was taken away on a recovery truck. Goalkeeper keeps his helmet on to stay incognito Sanchez seemed keen to avoid being recognised, with onlookers only realising who he was after spotting his name on the side of the car. The witness said: "He was wearing his normal clothes and a racing helmet. He didn't take his helmet off for some time. It was like he wanted to remain incognito, a bit like Stig. Even when the car got delivered back to the car park, he didn't want to take his helmet off for some reason." The Nurburgring, nicknamed 'The Green Hell' by Sir Jackie Stewart, was the scene of Niki Lauda's horrific crash in 1976. What's next for Sanchez at Como? Sanchez joined Cesc Fabregas' Como on loan in the summer after a difficult start to the Premier League season, but he has made just three Serie A appearances out of a possible nine. But then Manchester United happened to the best-laid plans. According to multiple sources in the UK, Pochettino has been identified as the man to haul Old Trafford out of its latest crisis . United will have to pay compensation in the region of $10m to get Pochettino out of his U.S. Soccer contract, with further recompense due for his coaching staff. item.content:encoded: Mauricio Pochettino replacements: Best fits for USMNT if manager bolts for Manchester United originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a feel-good World Cup on home soil and a long-term contract committing Mauricio Pochettino to summer 2030, the USMNT was all set for the medium to long term. The September international break gave us the first look at a youthful roster honing their skills under one of the most respected coaches of modern times. But then Manchester United happened to the best-laid plans. According to multiple sources in the UK, Pochettino has been identified as the man to haul Old Trafford out of its latest crisis . United will have to pay compensation in the region of $10m to get Pochettino out of his U.S. Soccer contract, with further recompense due for his coaching staff. So who will the United States federation invest in next at this crucial juncture? MORE: Man United on brink of sacking Michael Carrick with USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino lined up as replacement Canidates to replace Mauricio Pochettino as USMNT manager Pep Guardiola First up, let's get the moonshot out of the way. Guardiola is on sabbatical after a decade at Manchester City , so he would need to be persuaded to come back to work ahead of schedule. He would also not come cheap. But this isn't a non-starter. When Guardiola last took time out of club management for the duration of the 2012/13 season, he lived in New York and has an affinity for the United States. He also wants to take on an international job before the end of his career. Managing his native Spain would appear to be out of the question on account of Guardiola's support for Catalan self-determination. England are tied up with Thomas Tuchel until Euro 2028, and Guardiola knocked back enquiries from Italy last summer, doubling down on his intentions to take a break. It means there might be a window of opportunity for U.S. Soccer to make the case to the most influential coach of the 21st century to shape and guide a new era with a long-term vision. Getty Images Roberto Martinez A far more attainable Spanish coach, Martinez has become a specialist in the international game through long spells in charge of Belgium and Portugal over the past decade. He was mentioned in dispatches when Pochettino's long-term future was a matter of speculation prior to the World Cup. Being used to the pace of international management is definitely a plus, and Martinez can point to overseeing several solid tournament showings, most notably when he guided Belgium to the semifinals of the 2018 World Cup. At the same time, plenty of critics feel he squandered the full potential of two golden generations with the Red Devils and the Selecao. Steve Cherundolo If United wrap up their swoop for Pochettino in quick time, U.S. Under-23 coach Cherundolo would likely step in on an interim basis for the upcoming doubleheader against Haiti. Cherundolo getting the job long-term might feel like a cop-out of convenience from U.S. Soccer, but plenty of nations around the world can point to the benefits of appointing someone already in the building. Luis de la Fuente's successes with Spain are a prime example of this. Admittedly, Cherundolo has only been in post since July, and his elevation would necessitate a reworking of USA men's plans for the 2028 Olympic Games. But this 47-year-old, well-respected former international showed his chops when his LAFC claimed the Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup in 2022. There are certainly far worse options. Mikey Varas Another decent "company man" option, Varas was in charge of the USA Under-20 side from 2021 to 2023, when he won the CONCACAF U-20 Championship in 2022 and led his team to the quarterfinals of the 2023 FIFA U-20 Championship. He also worked as an assistant for the senior side and took charge of two matches as interim before Pochettino's appointment was confirmed in 2024. The 43-year-old Californian is currently in charge of San Diego FC, which finished top of the Western Conference on its MLS debut in 2025. They missed out on the postseason this time around. Getty Images B.J. Callaghan Callaghan served as USMNT interim head coach in 2023, taking charge of the CONCACAF Nations League Finals campaign and winning the trophy before Gregg Berhalter returned. But the 45-year-old's case can now primarily be made on the back of his superb work at Nashville SC. In his first full season in 2025, Callaghan oversaw 22 single-season wins and a streak of 15 games unbeaten across all competitions – both franchise records. They also collected the U.S. Open Cup. 2026 in Nashville has been a revelation. Callaghan's side are heavy favourites to lift the MLS Cup after setting a record regular season points tally of 77, with 23 wins and just three defeats. MORE: What Man City guilty verdict means for Pep Guardiola's legacy Rudi Garcia Perhaps U.S. Soccer could go for the man who beat the man. It's fair to say that if the U.S. had reached the quarterfinals or beyond at the 2026 World Cup, Pochettino's stock would have been high enough to land a prime job without Manchester United plunging back into crisis. But he didn't. He was outcoached by Rudi Garcia, whose Belgium ran out 4-1 winners before falling to Spain in the next round. They were the only team to score against Spain in the entire tournament. This marked a surprising upturn for Garcia, whose career had been beset by high-profile failures over recent years. He and Belgium parted company at the end of the World Cup. The opportunity to stay in the international game would probably appeal. Getty Images Wilfried Nancy Another French candidate after Garcia. And, if we're honest, one who might not prove any more popular with fans. Nancy did a superb job when he led Columbus Crew to the MLS Cup in 2023. He followed that up with the Leagues Cup in 2024, when he was also named MLS Coach of the Year. Nancy is currently available and has not worked since a reputation-shredding month in charge of Scottish giants Celtic from December 2025 to January this year, when he won two and lost six of eight matches. There would be concerns over whether Nancy could impart his detail-heavy take on positional play with the fleeting time available to an international coach.

item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. item.content:encoded: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. The 36-year-old Holiday, who would be a more natural complement next to Lillard or Morant than they are to each other, made his own case for why the point guard rotation makes sense. “It’s about being a complete basketball player for myself,” he said, “and I think we have a lot of guys like that.” There is a long history of teams talking themselves into superstar additions that make little sense. The Los Angeles Lakers once made a conscious decision to acquire Russell Westbrook and pair him with LeBron James. Nobody made them do that! The talent and star power of a Lillard-Morant backcourt is undeniable. Still, I remain unconvinced that Cronin, with a very hands-on new owner in his ear, made the deal with winning basketball games at the front of mind. Although, admittedly, Cronin’s biggest wins as a GM have been in the trade market. The haul of assets he collected for Lillard, only to get him back two years later, will go down as an all-time great swindle. So, too, will the oft-questioned Avdija trade a year later. Maybe he sees something in a Lillard-Morant pairing that many of us can’t. Morant could return to the All-Star form he had achieved before injuries and off-court issues derailed his ascent . And if he does, the Blazers can either trade him for pieces that fit better or clear out the logjam and build around him. But to sell the current roster as a basketball strategy doesn’t quite pass the smell test. Neither Lillard nor Morant has achieved stardom due to his defensive acumen. Each player needs the ball in his hands to thrive. If the duo is on the floor together, Avdija is no longer the secondary playmaker, he becomes tertiary. So, you are left to wonder whether the Blazers sold themselves on Morant because of how he can help the current collection of talent or if they simply saw the opportunity to land a 27-year-old All-NBA talent for cheap, regardless of what it meant for the existing roster construction. And if you’re being honest, you probably don’t need to wonder which of the two it is. “We were very focused and we’ll continue to be on … adding to our talent base as much as we can,” Cronin said. That thinking right there may tell you just how far ahead of everyone else the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are in the Western Conference. They are positioned to dominate for the next half-decade, if not longer. The only chance any other team has of disrupting that is taking bold risks. But I thought the goal was to go all in on the twilight years of Lillard’s career? “Dame literally just wants to win,” said first-year head coach Micah Nori, whose charge is to sort out arguably the most talented glut of point guard talent in NBA history. “I think that’s the only thing left he really has to (do). He’s already proven he’s a winner, but at the highest level.” Does adding Morant move Lillard closer to a title? Or simply give Portland a potential off-ramp if Lillard is no longer the same player after tearing his Achilles tendon? Morant was without question a low-risk, high-reward addition. He came at the reasonable price of Jerami Grant and Kris Murray. If it becomes clear that Morant is one point guard too many, or that he’s just not the player he once was, some will argue that it didn’t cost the Blazers much to try. However, there is an opportunity cost to messing with Lillard’s swan song. If you don’t get it right, you risk wasting the gift of his voluntary return last summer . And, not for nothing, Lillard has the option to become a free agent again after this season. The franchise icon certainly hasn’t said anything that would suggest he is unhappy about Morant’s presence, although he stopped short on Monday of a full-throated endorsement. He said he knew about the trade before it went through. When I asked if he thought it was a good idea right away or if he needed time to get on board with the plan, Lillard said, “My position on it was, I’m prepared for whatever.” It’s good that he’s already thinking about other positions. Because his old one is getting awfully crowded. Read the original article on oregonlive.com . Add oregonlive.com as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. Because we didn’t create success for our team this season.” Latest Ducks news Oregon makes a big leap in latest College Football Playoff rankings Dan Lanning backs expanded college football playoff to 24 teams Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham takes shot at Oregon’s $50M roster Read the original article on oregonlive.com . item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Arsenal youngster makes England u19 debut
item.description: Arsenal youngster makes England u19 debut Arsenal’s Marli Salmon made his debut for the England u19s on Wednesday, playing the full 90 minutes of an emphatic win over Slovenia. Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images Arsenal youth defender Marli Salmon was initially called up to the England u18s for the November international break, but he was quickly promoted to the u19s after a withdrawal. Far from just making up the numbers, Salmon immediately stepped into the starting lineup for England’s game against Slovenia on Wednesday. The match was an u19 European Championship qualifier, the second round of qualifiers. The top-three teams from each group will progress to the third round, with the entire second round of group matches to be played over the November break. Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images England got their second round of qualifiers off to the best possible start with a 4-1 win, with Reigan Heskey scoring a brace, Blaz Kovac netting an own goal, and substitute Harry Howell netting a fourth. The scoreline perhaps should have been even more emphatic, with Chizaram Ezenwata and Luca Williams-Barnett both missing penalties. Ezenwata hit the post, whilst Williams-Barnett was left embarrassed as his chipped effort was saved. Though Slovenia did get on the scoresheet, Salmon will be pleased to have debuted in a comfortable victory, as he played the full 90 minutes of the match. Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images England are now already in a strong position to progress, but they’ll want to remain professional and get results in their other two games against Belarus and Austria . The Belarus game is on November 14th at 12:00 GMT, and the Austria match is on November 17th at 13:00 GMT. If Salmon can continue to make a positive impression in those two games, there’s every chance he’ll find himself becoming a permanent member of the u19 squad. item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes guard Jaloni Cambridge (22) shoots in front of Howard Bison forward Sa'lah Hemingway (11) during the first round of the NCAA women's basketball tournament at the Jerome Schottenstein Center in Columbus on March 21, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The one stat that follows Ohio State women’s basketball is that they made it to the Second Round of the NCAA Tournament for three straight years, only to lose on home court. After consecutive tough ends to Buckeye seasons, media and voters have been hesitant to shower the Scarlet and Gray with any preseason praise. Fortunately for head coach Kevin McGuff’s side, praise does not win basketball games. However, point guard Jaloni Cambridge is responsible for winning a game or two in her two years at Ohio State. Now in year three, how has the guard improved her game and how far can she take the Buckeyes? Name: Jaloni Cambridge Position: Guard Class: Junior High School: Montverde Academy H.S. (Montverde, Florida) 2025-26 Stats: 23.2 ppg, 5.6 rpg, 4.4 apg, 49.4 FG%, 36.0 3PT FG%, 82.4 FT% Last Season Cambridge entered the 25-26 with team leadership firmly in her hands. The point guard’s freshman season was a crash course of learning to adjust to the size of college players and learning to play alongside other athletes who were also the big names at their high schools and academies. From the performances Cambridge exhibited last season, it was clear that she was trying to do it all for the Buckeyes. Cambridge led the team in scoring in 26 of 32 games and all but five Big Ten games. In seven matchups, Cambridge scored at least 30 points and twice scored 41 points. Those games were also not against mid-majors in the non-conference schedule. Six of the seven games were against Power Four opponents, which included the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in the NCAA Tournament’s Second Round. The first came against the Illinois Fighting Illini when the point guard completely took over the second half against another young and talented side led by then sophomore Berry Wallace. In front of Cambridge’s favorite WNBA player A’ja Wilson, who sat court side at the game in Champaign, Illinois, Cambridge was unstoppable in the second half. item.content:encoded: Ohio State Buckeyes guard Jaloni Cambridge (22) shoots in front of Howard Bison forward Sa'lah Hemingway (11) during the first round of the NCAA women's basketball tournament at the Jerome Schottenstein Center in Columbus on March 21, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The one stat that follows Ohio State women’s basketball is that they made it to the Second Round of the NCAA Tournament for three straight years, only to lose on home court. After consecutive tough ends to Buckeye seasons, media and voters have been hesitant to shower the Scarlet and Gray with any preseason praise. Fortunately for head coach Kevin McGuff’s side, praise does not win basketball games. However, point guard Jaloni Cambridge is responsible for winning a game or two in her two years at Ohio State. Now in year three, how has the guard improved her game and how far can she take the Buckeyes? Name: Jaloni Cambridge Position: Guard Class: Junior High School: Montverde Academy H.S. (Montverde, Florida) 2025-26 Stats: 23.2 ppg, 5.6 rpg, 4.4 apg, 49.4 FG%, 36.0 3PT FG%, 82.4 FT% Last Season Cambridge entered the 25-26 with team leadership firmly in her hands. The point guard’s freshman season was a crash course of learning to adjust to the size of college players and learning to play alongside other athletes who were also the big names at their high schools and academies. From the performances Cambridge exhibited last season, it was clear that she was trying to do it all for the Buckeyes. Cambridge led the team in scoring in 26 of 32 games and all but five Big Ten games. In seven matchups, Cambridge scored at least 30 points and twice scored 41 points. Those games were also not against mid-majors in the non-conference schedule. Six of the seven games were against Power Four opponents, which included the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in the NCAA Tournament’s Second Round. The first came against the Illinois Fighting Illini when the point guard completely took over the second half against another young and talented side led by then sophomore Berry Wallace. In front of Cambridge’s favorite WNBA player A’ja Wilson, who sat court side at the game in Champaign, Illinois, Cambridge was unstoppable in the second half. All season, Cambridge showed that the moment was never too big. Against the Michigan Wolverines, down three points with less than one second left, Cambridge got to the foul line and hit all three free throws to get the Buckeyes to overtime, where the Wolverines ultimately capitalized on a rushed final offensive possession by Ohio State. Through the play of Cambridge, the Buckeyes were one of only two Big Ten teams to play within 10 points of the eventual national champions in the UCLA Bruins. Although in the Big Ten Tournament against the Bruins, Cambridge was caught doing too much for the Buckeyes and head coach Cori Close was ready through center Lauren Betts. The 6-foot-7 center who won the Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year was on Cambridge when she went inside and made the game difficult for the then sophomore. Even so, the success of a fourth place finish in a competitive Big Ten conference for a team full of underclassmen points back to the play of Cambridge. The point guard ended the season atop the Big Ten scoring numbers with 813 points and 23.2 points per game. It earned her spots on the Coaches and Media First Team All-Big Ten and an Associated Press Second Team All-American honor. What to Expect A better question for Cambridge is what not to expect from the dynamic junior. At 5’7, she can’t dunk. That’s about it. Cambridge is still a three-level scorer, she is still fast and she still plays strong on the defensive end of the court. What will be different is the guard’s strength overall. In the offseason, the guard said she spent more time in the gym lifting weights than she did on the basketball court, which means a lot considering the work she puts in on the practice court. “I really made an emphasis to get stronger this year, and it’ll definitely show on my body,” Cambridge told reporters. “I felt great, and the results from just like with our strength coach Claire [Quebedeaux]. I mean, you should really see my numbers from last year to this year. I feel faster. I feel so much better than I did last year, and I’m healthier now. So with my Achilles and everything, everything feels good.” The guard’s offensive focuses are on deep shooting and assists. Cambridge was not satisfied with her 3.9 attempted three-point shots per game and 36.0% of her attempts. That has already bumped up after only three games of the 26-27 regular season. Cambridge attempted 5.7 shots from deep and hit 2.0 per game. Against the Central Michigan University Chippewas, Cambridge showed she is still fine with taking over a game sometimes. Cambridge she scored 15 points in the first quarter on 4-of-5 shooting and she still added in four assists. Also expect a jump in leadership ability. Ohio State was young last year and it was a crash course for the then sophomore point guard. In year three, the poise of being a leader and running the game on and off the court shows in Cambridge, but granted it came against sides where the Scarlet and Gray did not face a lot of adversity. Prediction It is hard to imagine Jaloni Cambridge being better, but in year two of being a formal leader on the roster, she will impact games even more. There will still be blistering runs to the basket but Cambridge’s game will be smarter. The point guard won’t force her game inside but instead force opponents to adjust to her adjustments. If the team around Cambridge stays healthy, the offensive load will not solely be atop her shoulders, like it was last season. The two key areas to watch in Cambridge’s growth will be how she gets those teammates involved in games. It is still far too early to say its worked but the guard’s assists are up from 4.4 last season to 6.0 per game in the 26-27 season. Also, the guard’s scoring is down, but Cambridge will tell anyone who asks that a win with her scoring less points is better than a loss with her atop the stat sheet in the points column. An added source of motivation for Cambridge is playing her last season alongside sister Kennedy Cambridge. Now, Jaloni Cambridge does not need much in the motivation department but the two said their goal is to get to at least the Sweet Sixteen. There is also a pair of big games in Columbus in March when Nationwide Arena hosts the Final Four a few miles away from the Ohio State campus. Jaloni Cambridge has the ability to lead the program to new heights, but she won’t be able to do it alone. Highlights Watch highlights from Cambridge’s career high scoring game against the Illinois Fighting Illini. Miss any player previews? Here’s the list so far: Ava Watson Adriana Díaz Sydney Mobley Kennedy Cambridge Bryn Martin Ella Hobbs Atlee Vanesko Seini Henry Kylee Kitts Elsa Lemmilä

item.title: Mercedes explains "unusual" car behaviour behind Kimi Antonelli's costly Interlagos spin
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord In his first event since his maiden title was confirmed in Mexico, Antonelli looked set to capitalise on a poor start by polesitter Lando Norris to snatch the lead from second on the grid, building up a comfortable buffer over the first 15 laps of a wet-dry-wet race. But after changing from worn intermediates to slicks on lap 18, in response to Norris' stop one lap prior, Antonelli began reporting puzzling suspension issues, feeling like his W17 was pulling to one side. Two laps later Antonelli went off in Turn 1 as his car's rear end suddenly snapped under braking, spitting Antonelli out into the run-off area. The Italian recovered but lost the lead to Norris and dropped further down the order to finish fifth, 41 seconds behind Norris. Antonelli's spin didn't come in isolation, as he had already gone off at the slippery Turn 12. Meanwhile, team-mate George Russell was fortunate to survive a spin at the narrow pit exit as he rallied to finish ahead of Antonelli in fourth. "The spin is something I need to look at because I don't know why I lost the rear so quickly as well," Antonelli said after his anger over his poor race had subsided thanks to Mercedes clinching the constructors' title. "Like no warning, nothing. But already when I put on the softs, I felt something weird with the car. So, we need to check what happened but on the other hand yeah, shame because we lost the race there." Mercedes clinched its first constructors' title since 2021 Mercedes clinched its first constructors' title since 2021 After investigating the handling issues both of its drivers experienced, Mercedes believes the handling anomalies they reported were largely down to the difficulties getting the tyres into the right operating window in Sunday's cooler conditions. "Kimi obviously had had a spin, flat-spotted all four tyres and so his pace was somewhat limited," said Lord in the team's social media debrief. "We did really struggle as we went onto that dry soft tyre and then in the final inter-stint as well, with a car that was very, very tricky to drive, very oversteery and in the soft tyre stint in particular, with very low tyre temperatures. "That meant both of the drivers, and indeed other drivers in the field, actually thought there was something broken with the car. But looking at it, it looked like we were just below the tyre temperature window, sometimes popping into it, but then dropping back out of it in the damp conditions, and that's what was causing the very strange and unusual car behaviour." Lord added: "It was a really topsy-turvy race. It's not very often that you spin off on a formation lap and almost make contact with a barrier, that you spin in the pitlane with the other car, that you have several incidents on track as well and nonetheless manage to come home fourth and fifth. item.title: San Joaquin County girls volleyball CIF State first-round scores, recap
item.description: A first-round home game is one thing. Winning it in the CIF State playoffs? That's another. Because at this point in the season, there are no easy opponents . The field is filled with some of California's best girls volleyball programs, and the difference between seeds doesn't always tell the whole story. Four San Joaquin County teams had the opportunity to begin their state championship journeys at home Tuesday, Nov. 10. And despite the level of competition, all four made the most of it. Here's how each team fared in the opening round of the CIF State girls volleyball playoffs, along with the scores and a full recap. Division II No. 1 St. Mary's 3, No. 16 Cardinal Newman 2 Earning the No. 1 seed comes with expectations. For a program with five Northern California championships, 14 Sac-Joaquin Section titles and 32 league championships, St. Mary's knows those expectations well. But against Cardinal Newman, the North Bay-Oak League champion, living up to them took everything the Rams had. St. Mary's came from behind to secure a dramatic 19-25, 25-16, 25-17, 22-25, 15-13 victory. A team that finished the regular season with 80 consecutive TCAL wins suddenly found itself in unfamiliar territory, trailing 11-9 and later 13-12 in the deciding set. For a closer look at how St. Mary's survived, read The Record's full game story. Division III No. 3 Ripon 3, No. 14 Washington 0 For five straight years, Ripon has reached a section championship game. And for five straight years, that has earned the Indians a spot in the state tournament. But until Tuesday, one thing had been missing. A state tournament victory. Ripon finally checked that box with a 25-21, 25-21, 25-10 sweep of San Francisco's Washington, which entered 23-8 after placing third in the Academic Athletic Association at 11-3. The Indians, ranked No. 70 in California by MaxPreps compared with Washington's No. 233 ranking, got another strong performance from junior outside hitter Ashlyn Malone, who followed her 18-kill section championship outing with 12 kills, six digs and two aces. Freshman outside hitter Lilia Tuputala added 11 kills, senior opposite Jorie Eskes had nine, and senior setter Alayna Sprinkle finished with 27 assists and 10 digs after recording 41 assists in the section final. Senior libero Kennedy Everhart anchored the defense with 23 digs. Division IV No. 2 Escalon 3, No. 15 Quincy 0 Experience can make all the difference in the state playoffs, and Escalon has plenty of it. A year after reaching the state regional semifinals, the Cougars returned many of the players who helped make that run possible. They put that experience to work against Quincy, sweeping a team that entered with 37 wins, three losses and an undefeated 10-0 Mid-Valley League record, 25-13, 25-16, 25-19. Quincy hadn't lost since Aug. 22 until the Northern Section Division II championship, but Escalon made it two straight defeats. The Indians, ranked No. 70 in California by MaxPreps compared with Washington's No. 233 ranking, got another strong performance from junior outside hitter Ashlyn Malone, who followed her 18-kill section championship outing with 12 kills, six digs and two aces. Freshman outside hitter Lilia Tuputala added 11 kills, senior opposite Jorie Eskes had nine, and senior setter Alayna Sprinkle finished with 27 assists and 10 digs after recording 41 assists in the section final. Senior libero Kennedy Everhart anchored the defense with 23 digs. Quincy hadn't lost since Aug. 22 until the Northern Section Division II championship, but Escalon made it two straight defeats. Sophomore Avery Bartelink led with 10 kills, 10 digs, two aces and a block, while senior setter Aniston Hunt distributed 30 assists to go with 12 digs, an ace and a kill. Junior outside hitter Emma Strong added nine kills, six digs, an ace and a block, senior opposite and middle hitter Haven MacKinnon had six kills, five digs, an ace and a block, and senior libero Brynn Caton contributed eight digs, three aces and three assists. No. 6 Ripon Christian 3, No. 11 West Valley 0 Wins have a funny way of losing their importance once the postseason begins. On paper, the records suggested one thing. The seeding suggested another. And Ripon Christian showed why it was the No. 6 seed, cruising to a 25-13, 25-18, 25-19 sweep. Senior opposite and outside hitter Alyssa Hofman led the Knights with seven kills, 14 digs and three aces, while senior setters Brooklynn Postma and Rhian Heuvel contributed 12 and 10 assists, respectively. item.title: 'Couldn't be a more brain-dead decision': Craig Carton chides Dianna Russini over BetUS deal
item.description: Credit: OutKick, Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Craig Carton knows a thing or two about the perils of gambling, and he’s not happy about Dianna Russini’s alignment with online gambling company BetUS. Russini is making her long-awaited return to the sports media world on Wednesday with the debut of a weekly live show for BetUS . It’s a curious landing spot for the former ESPN and The Athletic NFL insider . Her reporting career came crashing down earlier this year following allegations of an intimate relationship with NFL head coach Mike Vrabel, but it was always assumed she’d resurface. Even then, it was presumed that if a mainstream media outlet didn’t want to take a chance on her, one of the major sports betting platforms or prediction markets would add her to their list of sports-centric hosts they’ve been throwing money at. For whatever reason, Russini ended up working with the lesser-known BetUS, for whom The Russini Report will be its most high-profile show by a mile. Carton, whose own sports media career was rocked by scandal, knows quite a bit about the sports betting world. His initial stint with WFAN ended when a gambling addiction led to his arrest for securities and wire fraud. He eventually found his way back to WFAN (for a third time) with The Carton Show with Craig Carton & Chris McMonigle , and he’s spent a lot of time speaking out about the dangers of gambling addiction and the many ways the industry takes advantage of people. He did not mince words when discussing Russini and her partnership with BetUS on his show. Carton’s take on Dianna Russini partnering with an illegal sports book. He’s 100% right. She is so dumb. https://t.co/PJkrNpgIzO — DJ Joey DiSarno (@DJJoeyDiSarno) November 10, 2026 “She partnered with BetUS. BetUS doesn’t have any operations in the U.S. BetUS is an illegal sportsbook in Curaçao. It is not regulated or licensed in a single state in this country. Now, it’s not illegal to bet with them, but if you do, you’re never going to see your money. They do these rollover plans. ‘Hey, it’s nice that you won, but you got to bet it 5 more times.’ Got a 1.5 stars on the Better Business Bureau rating.” It’s true that BetUS operates entirely offshore, with headquarters in San José, Costa Rica. It’s also true that BetUS does not hold a gaming license from any U.S. state regulator, and several states have issued cease-and-desist orders or fines against them for offering illegal online gambling to their residents. It is also correct that BetUS is licensed and regulated by the government of Curaçao , which essentially means nothing to regulators in the United States. item.content:encoded: Credit: OutKick, Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Craig Carton knows a thing or two about the perils of gambling, and he’s not happy about Dianna Russini’s alignment with online gambling company BetUS. Russini is making her long-awaited return to the sports media world on Wednesday with the debut of a weekly live show for BetUS . It’s a curious landing spot for the former ESPN and The Athletic NFL insider . Her reporting career came crashing down earlier this year following allegations of an intimate relationship with NFL head coach Mike Vrabel, but it was always assumed she’d resurface. Even then, it was presumed that if a mainstream media outlet didn’t want to take a chance on her, one of the major sports betting platforms or prediction markets would add her to their list of sports-centric hosts they’ve been throwing money at. For whatever reason, Russini ended up working with the lesser-known BetUS, for whom The Russini Report will be its most high-profile show by a mile. Carton, whose own sports media career was rocked by scandal, knows quite a bit about the sports betting world. His initial stint with WFAN ended when a gambling addiction led to his arrest for securities and wire fraud. He eventually found his way back to WFAN (for a third time) with The Carton Show with Craig Carton & Chris McMonigle , and he’s spent a lot of time speaking out about the dangers of gambling addiction and the many ways the industry takes advantage of people. He did not mince words when discussing Russini and her partnership with BetUS on his show. Carton’s take on Dianna Russini partnering with an illegal sports book. He’s 100% right. She is so dumb. https://t.co/PJkrNpgIzO — DJ Joey DiSarno (@DJJoeyDiSarno) November 10, 2026 “She partnered with BetUS. BetUS doesn’t have any operations in the U.S. BetUS is an illegal sportsbook in Curaçao. It is not regulated or licensed in a single state in this country. Now, it’s not illegal to bet with them, but if you do, you’re never going to see your money. They do these rollover plans. ‘Hey, it’s nice that you won, but you got to bet it 5 more times.’ Got a 1.5 stars on the Better Business Bureau rating.” It’s true that BetUS operates entirely offshore, with headquarters in San José, Costa Rica. It’s also true that BetUS does not hold a gaming license from any U.S. state regulator, and several states have issued cease-and-desist orders or fines against them for offering illegal online gambling to their residents. It is also correct that BetUS is licensed and regulated by the government of Curaçao , which essentially means nothing to regulators in the United States. Carton chided Russini over her presumed effort not to discuss the details around the scandal that rocked her career, as well as the guest list for her first show (Bill Parcells, Damon Amendalora, Spike Eskin), before bringing it back to BetUS’s shady standing. “You announce that of all the gambling sites that people use in this country, you’ve chose none of them and instead are working with BetUS, which is an illegal sportsbook in this country. Again, it’s not illegal to place the bet. They just can’t take US money. And they do. You also cannot use a credit card to make deposits there. It’s all cryptocurrency. Or Western Union. “So that is a horrendous choice for your first partner. But I get it. They wrote you a check.” Aligning with BetUS in her return to the sports media world raises a lot of questions for Dianna Russini. Add it to the list of things she probably needs to offer some context for, but may try not to do. The post Craig Carton chides Dianna Russini over BetUS deal: ‘Couldn’t be a more brain-dead decision’ appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Former top recruit among Commodores to know vs. Vanderbilt in Week 11
item.description: The Vanderbilt Commodores have certainly given the Alabama Crimson Tide problems each of the last two seasons. Led by quarterback Diego Pavia, Vanderbilt stunned the Crimson Tide in Nashville during the 2024 season, 40-35, a result which snapped a lengthy losing streak in the series. Vanderbilt then gave the Tide problems once again a year ago in Tuscaloosa as well, with Alabama eventually pulling away in the second half to avenge that 2024 loss, 30-14. This season, Vanderbilt will face the Crimson Tide with a 4-5 (1-5 SEC) record that has seen the Commodores drop five of their last six games. The Commodores are still led by head coach Clark Lea, and sport a roster that features a number of players who have faced Alabama before, as well as some who have not, in key positions. Here are five Vanderbilt Commodores to know ahead of Week 11 , as well as how each has performed before against the Tide. Jared Curtis, Quarterback Vanderbilt's starting quarterback is Jared Curtis, a true freshman who has completed 64.7% of his passes for 1,657 yards and an 8:8 TD:INT ratio over eight games this season. A top recruit in the 2026 high school class, Curtis also has 76 rushes for 172 yards and two touchdowns this season, and is set to face Alabama for the first time. Junior Sherrill, Wide Receiver Junior Sherrill is undoubtedly Vanderbilt's top pass catching option who currently leads the Commodores with 747 yards and four touchdowns this season on 56 receptions. The senior wideout is also averaging 23.8 yards over six kick returns this season, and is set to face Alabama for the third time. Sherrill has a combined eight receptions for 94 yards and a touchdown against the Tide over the last two seasons. CJ Heard, Safety CJ Heard is leading the Vanderbilt defense with 64 total tackles this season, 44 of which have been solo, while also having recorded four TFL, three sacks, one interception, six pass defenses, and two forced fumbles. The junior had eight tackles, six of which were solo, against the Crimson Tide a year ago. Sedrick Alexander, Running Back The Commodores' leading rusher is Sedrick Alexander with 333 yards and six touchdowns on 85 carries, while the senior also has 17 receptions for 153 yards and another score this season. Over the last two years, Alexander has rushed for a combined 140 yards and three touchdowns on 25 attempts against Alabama. The running back also had five receptions for 46 yards and another touchdown as a receiver. Nick Rinaldi, Linebacker Nick Rinaldi is another name on the Vanderbilt defense enjoying a solid season with 58 total tackles, 29 of which have been solo, as well as 5.5 TFL, 3.5 sacks, and five pass defenses. The graduate student linebacker has five tackles, one TFL, one sack, and a pass defense in two career games against Alabama. item.title: Fantasy Football Week 10 Start ’Em, Sit ’Em: Audric Estime, Jalen Coker And More
item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 8: Audric Estime #30 of the New Orleans Saints warms up before a game against the Cleveland Browns at Caesars Superdome on November 8, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We have now hit Week 10 of the fantasy football season, and we’ll be talking about key starts and sits once again. If you want a recap of the rules, you can read the last article linked here , but the goal is to not just select obvious names. As for the rankings that are used, it will be the FantasyPros expert consensus PPR rankings from Week 10. Fantasy Football Week 10 RB Start: Audric Estime (RB24) There’s definitely risk in starting Audric Estime this week, but he’s coming off a very good performance against the Cleveland Browns. Estime had 14.7 points with 15 carries last week, which indicates that he should have a large workload once again. The encouraging sign to me is that the Browns have allowed the 15th most PPG to running backs this year, but the Panthers have allowed the 2nd most. With a great matchup, Estime is worth starting. Fantasy Football Week 10 RB Sit: Woody Marks (RB18) With Woody Marks, he’s struggled this year, and there’s not really much of an upside case either. Marks had his best game with 12.5 points in week five, and over his last three performances, his production has declined every time. Last week, Marks scored 8.4 points, and he faces the Browns, who are a fine matchup as mentioned above. Fantasy Football Week 10 WR Start: Carnell Tate (WR26) The hope is that after missing Week 8, Carnell Tate should be back and ready to go this week. The linked report seems to indicate that is the case as of now. With Tate, the hope is that he improves over the season as a rookie, and we’ve already seen that elite upside as shown in Week 4 with 21.5 points and Week 6 with 19. I’m good to start Tate because, since Week 4, he’s had at least five targets in every game, with seven or more in all but one. Tate has also scored at least 9.9 points in three of his last four games as well. Tate now goes up against the Jacksonville Jaguars, who allowed the 15th most PPG to the position. Fantasy Football Week 10 WR Sit: Jalen Coker (WR20) Jalen Coker had a big start to the year, but since Week 7, he’s been fairly underwhelming. Not only has Coker failed to cross 10 points since Week 6, but he hasn’t had over six targets since either. Between that and the New Orleans Saints allowing the 16th most PPG to wide receivers, I’m looking to sit Coker this week. Fantasy Football Week 10 WR Sit: Jalen Coker (WR20) Jalen Coker had a big start to the year, but since Week 7, he’s been fairly underwhelming. Not only has Coker failed to cross 10 points since Week 6, but he hasn’t had over six targets since either. Between that and the New Orleans Saints allowing the 16th most PPG to wide receivers, I’m looking to sit Coker this week. Fantasy Football Week 10 QB Start: Bryce Young (QB13) With Bryce Young, he had a rough stretch of scoring under 11 points from week 7 to week 8, but came back with 20.3 points in week 9. Young did this against the Denver Broncos, who allowed the 17th most PPG to quarterbacks this year, and now Young takes on the New Orleans Saints. With the Saints being an even better matchup, allowing the 12th most PPG, this makes me excited to start Young right now. Fantasy Football Week 10 QB Sit: Jordan Love (QB11) Typically, I don’t like to sit players after constantly producing, and Jordan Love is coming off a 36.2 point game. Love is also averaging 20.6 PPG this year, but the problem is the matchup. In this case, it’s the fact that the Minnesota Vikings have been such a bad matchup for opposing quarterbacks, clearly allowing the least PPG to the position at 9.5. Fantasy Football Week 10 TE Start: Darren Waller (TE15) Darren Waller is not a safe play, but he is averaging 9.6 PPG this year. There are two sides of the coin with this one. Waller has four games with at least 10 points, and he scored 18.3 or more in two of them. One of those came last week, when Waller had 23 points. On the other hand, Waller has scored 6.6 points or fewer in those other four games. The reason why Waller makes sense to start now is that the Saints have allowed the 7th most PPG to tight ends this year. Fantasy Football Week 10 TE Sit: Tucker Kraft (TE12) Even though Tucker Kraft is a great player, after calling him a start last week, he scored just 1.9 points. Kraft hasn’t necessarily been someone you have to start each week this year, averaging 10 PPG in 2026. This time, Kraft is a good sit as he takes on the Vikings, who have allowed the fewest PPG to tight ends. Fantasy Football Week 10 D/ST Start: New Orleans Saints D/ST (D/ST11) The Saints’ defense has been solid in fantasy football, scoring 4.1 PPG. That said, the reason we’re looking to start them in Week 10 is the matchup. The Saints take on the Carolina Panthers, who have allowed the 7th most PPG to opposing D/ST’s this year. Fantasy Football Week 10 D/ST Sit: Green Bay Packers D/ST (D/ST4) As for the Packers, they’re the opposite. Green Bay is averaging 7.4 PPG, but they don’t have a great opponent in the Minnesota Vikings. Not only that, but the Vikings just got a quarterback upgrade with Kirk Cousins. The Vikings already ranked 12th in PPG allowed to the position in fantasy football this year. Assuming that Cousins is the starter, that should make the matchup even tougher. item.title: Re-analysis of black hole data proves iconic ring shape really is there
item.description: The original black hole image (left) and the new image (right) S. Lai, N. Thyagarajan, O. I. Wong, and F. Diakogiannis; Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation/EHT collaboration When the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) team released their first image of a black hole in 2019, the astrophysics community was abuzz: the image of black hole M87* showed a perfect ring structure, just as predicted by the theory of general relativity. As other teams reanalysed the data in the following years, though, scepticism about the image began to slip in. A new, completely independent analysis has now finally banished that scepticism. The now-iconic doughnut shape of the EHT image is caused by a key property of general relativity, the way that light bends in the presence of an extremely massive object. Observing it for real was one of the strongest pieces of evidence that general relativity is accurate. Read more Hubble Space Telescope is falling to Earth – should NASA save it? What allowed us to finally capture the image was the unique structure of the EHT, which is made up of a network of telescopes all around the world, used as one Earth-sized radio dish. This allows it to peer much closer to the edge of a black hole than any other observatory. However, the same structure that enabled the image also limits the EHT. “It has only a handful of telescopes spread across the globe, which leaves large gaps in its measurements that the imaging algorithm has to fill in,” says Nithyanandan Thyagarajan at CSIRO in Australia. “It also observes at very short radio wavelengths, where the atmosphere can distort the signal.” Advertisement These limitations mean that the raw data from the EHT is more subject to interpretation than most astronomical observations, and the way the data is processed is particularly impactful on the final image. Most of the analyses of the M87* data produced similar ring shapes, but one that was published in 2022 found no ring at all. So, when Thyagarajan and his colleagues reanalysed the data, they developed an entirely new data pipeline to do so. Instead of analysing the data from pairs of EHT telescopes before combining them, which is the standard method, they grouped the telescopes into triplets. Free newsletter Sign up to Launchpad Sign up to newsletter “By combining measurements from sets of three telescopes, we preserve the information about the object’s shape while cancelling out errors from the atmosphere and the telescopes,” says Thyagarajan. They also developed a machine learning algorithm trained on non-black-hole images to minimise bias from their own expectations of what the image might look like. In the end, their new image is nearly identical to the original. This is a key confirmation of the EHT’s finding that general relativity truly does describe the space-time around a black hole accurately. Journal Reference: Nature DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-11241-9

item.title: 'There's tremendous demand': Rocket Lab raises price of Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million
item.description: null The coming launch bottleneck has ramped up demand for a rocket that has yet to leave the ground. Rocket Lab announced on Monday (Nov. 9) that it recently raised the price of a Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million — an increase of more than 25%, for a ride on a rocket that's set to debut in 2027. "Launch is extremely constrained, and that is exactly the situation we predicted," Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck said on Monday during the company's third-quarter earnings call. "We saw a pent-up launch market on the horizon, and rather than provide early discounted launches, we set out to deliver a rocket into an environment with extreme demand at full price or higher." Rocket Lab is best known for Electron , a workhorse small-satellite launcher that debuted in 2017 and now has 90 orbital missions under its belt. The 59-foot-tall (18 meters) expendable rocket and can haul 660 pounds (300 kilograms) to low Earth orbit (LEO). Neutron is the company's entry into the medium-lift market. It features a reusable first stage, stands 141 feet (43 m) tall and can carry 14.3 tons (13 metric tons) of payload to LEO. Rocket Lab announced Neutron back in 2021 and first targeted a 2024 debut for the vehicle. But various problems have cropped up over the years, pushing things back. Last month, for example, Rocket Lab announced that it was delaying the first Neutron flight from late 2026 into 2027 due to a manufacturing issue (which it says is now under control). Such setbacks have not dampened demand for Neutron's services, however. During Monday's call, Beck revealed that Rocket Lab booked eight Neutron launches during the third quarter of 2026, which ran from July 1 through Sept. 30. The contracts for those eight flights are worth "a total of roughly 515 million, including multiple missions on a new escalated base price of $70 million," Beck said. Neutron's first 16 launches are now sold out, he added, and bookings from here on will be for flights in the 2030s. "The demand is a function of both a tightening global launch supply and our customers' confidence that Rocket Lab is the right partner to break the world's launch bottleneck," Beck said. Artist's illustration of Neutron's first stage coming down for a landing on a ship at sea. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) That bottleneck is coming in 2028 or so, when SpaceX plans to retire its Falcon 9 rocket . For some perspective, and comparison with Neutron: SpaceX currently charges $74 million for each Falcon 9 launch. The rocket has a reusable first stage and can carry about 25 tons (22.7 metric tons) to LEO. The medium lifter has been the world's most prolific rocket for the past few years. In 2025, for example, it flew 165 times — roughly the same number of orbital missions as all other launchers in the world combined. And all 165 of those flights were successful. But SpaceX is phasing out the Falcon 9 — and its heavy-lift cousin, the Falcon Heavy — nonetheless, shifting all launch work over to its f

Rocket Lab announced on Monday (Nov. 9) that it recently raised the price of a Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million — an increase of more than 25%, for a ride on a rocket that's set to debut in 2027. "Launch is extremely constrained, and that is exactly the situation we predicted," Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck said on Monday during the company's third-quarter earnings call. "We saw a pent-up launch market on the horizon, and rather than provide early discounted launches, we set out to deliver a rocket into an environment with extreme demand at full price or higher." Rocket Lab is best known for Electron , a workhorse small-satellite launcher that debuted in 2017 and now has 90 orbital missions under its belt. The 59-foot-tall (18 meters) expendable rocket and can haul 660 pounds (300 kilograms) to low Earth orbit (LEO). Neutron is the company's entry into the medium-lift market. It features a reusable first stage, stands 141 feet (43 m) tall and can carry 14.3 tons (13 metric tons) of payload to LEO. Rocket Lab announced Neutron back in 2021 and first targeted a 2024 debut for the vehicle. But various problems have cropped up over the years, pushing things back. Last month, for example, Rocket Lab announced that it was delaying the first Neutron flight from late 2026 into 2027 due to a manufacturing issue (which it says is now under control). Such setbacks have not dampened demand for Neutron's services, however. During Monday's call, Beck revealed that Rocket Lab booked eight Neutron launches during the third quarter of 2026, which ran from July 1 through Sept. 30. The contracts for those eight flights are worth "a total of roughly 515 million, including multiple missions on a new escalated base price of $70 million," Beck said. Neutron's first 16 launches are now sold out, he added, and bookings from here on will be for flights in the 2030s. "The demand is a function of both a tightening global launch supply and our customers' confidence that Rocket Lab is the right partner to break the world's launch bottleneck," Beck said. Artist's illustration of Neutron's first stage coming down for a landing on a ship at sea. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) That bottleneck is coming in 2028 or so, when SpaceX plans to retire its Falcon 9 rocket . For some perspective, and comparison with Neutron: SpaceX currently charges $74 million for each Falcon 9 launch. The rocket has a reusable first stage and can carry about 25 tons (22.7 metric tons) to LEO. The medium lifter has been the world's most prolific rocket for the past few years. In 2025, for example, it flew 165 times — roughly the same number of orbital missions as all other launchers in the world combined. And all 165 of those flights were successful. But SpaceX is phasing out the Falcon 9 — and its heavy-lift cousin, the Falcon Heavy — nonetheless, shifting all launch work over to its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which can haul more than 100 tons to LEO. There's a real worry among folks in the space community that this massive payload capacity won't be available to them for a while. SpaceX has made it pretty clear that early Starship operations will be geared toward internal priorities — specifically, the buildout of SpaceX's Starlink V3 broadband network and its Starmind AI data-center constellation. These will be very big jobs, even for the most powerful rocket ever built. For example, the Starlink V3 megaconstellation will consist of about 100,000 satellites , according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk . Starship can carry about 60 of these spacecraft to LEO per launch, so just building out the constellation will require about 1,700 liftoffs. The numbers for Starmind will be even more mind-boggling, for SpaceX wants that constellation to eventually harbor a million satellites . The coming launch bottleneck should increase demand for Electron as well as Neutron, Beck said during Monday's call. After all, many small-satellite operators have launched with SpaceX over the years, booking spots on Falcon 9 "rideshare" flights . And those opportunities are now drying up. "The next logical alternative is of course an Electron, so we see tremendous traction there," Beck said.
