item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: …reject fuel subsidy return, urge peaceful elections, commend new military formations in Oyo, Ekiti By Adeola Badru Traditional rulers from across the South-West have endorsed the continuation of the presidency in Southern Nigeria beyond the 2027 general elections, declaring that sustaining the principle of power rotation is critical to national unity, political stability, equity and inclusiveness. The monarchs also reaffirmed their unwavering support for President Bola Tinubu and his administration while backing the proposed establishment of state police as part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture. These were among the major resolutions reached at a meeting of the South-West Council of Obas and Traditional Rulers held at the Aafin Olubadan, Oke Aremo, Ibadan, Oyo State, on Wednesday. The meeting, which brought together prominent traditional rulers from the six South-West states, also endorsed the Federal Government’s position against the reintroduction of fuel subsidy, called for peaceful and credible elections in 2027, and urged greater collaboration among Nigeria’s geopolitical regions. In a communiqué issued and read by the Alake of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Gbadebo, at the end of the meeting, said the rotational presidency arrangement had contributed significantly to political stability, inclusiveness and national cohesion, stressing that the arrangement should be sustained in the next electoral cycle. The Council declared, “The principle of rotational presidency has, over the years, contributed significantly to political stability, inclusiveness, and national cohesion across Nigeria.” “In the interest of fairness, equity, and the continued strengthening of national unity, the Council expressed the view that the rotational arrangement should be sustained and that the presidency should remain in Southern Nigeria in the next electoral cycle, in line with the spirit of power rotation that has helped preserve peace and stability in the country.” The monarchs explained that their position was informed by the need to strengthen mutual trust among the federating units and preserve the delicate balance required for the country’s continued progress. They added that the position was intended to promote “national balance, mutual trust among the federating units, and the continued progress of the Nigerian State”. On the 2027 general elections, the traditional rulers called on political parties, candidates and the electorate to embrace democratic values and shun activities capable of undermining the electoral process. They condemned electoral violence, intimidation, vote-buying and other forms of electoral malpractice, emphasising the need for peaceful, free and credible elections at all levels. “The Council underscored the importance of peaceful, free, and credible elections at all levels. It condemned all forms of electoral violence, intimidation, vote-buying, and other electoral malpractices, urging political actors and citizens alike to uphold democratic values before, during, and after elections,” the communiqué stated. On national leadership, the monarchs unanimously reaffirmed their support for President Tinubu, acknowledging the efforts of the Federal Government in addressing the country’s challenges and advancing its development agenda. The Council also urged traditional rulers across the region to intensify grassroots mobilisation and sensitisation to encourage citizens to support government programmes and policies aimed at promoting economic growth, national stability and social development. “The Council unanimously reaffirmed its unwavering support for His Excellency, the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and his administration,” the communiqué stated. It added that the monarchs acknowledged the federal government’s efforts towards addressing national challenges and advancing the country’s development agenda. The Council’s position on the proposed state police initiative was equally emphatic, with the monarchs describing it as a strategic intervention capable of strengthening internal security and improving responses to security threats across the country. They urged traditional rulers to begin preparing and sensitising youths within their respective domains to take advantage of employment and other service opportunities that might emerge from the initiative. “The Council expressed support for the proposed establishment of State Police as a strategic measure to strengthen internal security,” the communiqué said. It further encouraged monarchs across the Southwest to prepare young people in their communities for opportunities that could arise from the proposed security arrangement. On the controversial fuel subsidy policy, the traditional rulers aligned themselves with the Federal Government’s current position, arguing that a return to the subsidy regime would not serve Nigeria’s long-term economic interests. While acknowledging the economic realities confronting the country, the monarchs maintained that fiscal sustainability and national economic development should remain central to policy decisions. “The Council noted the economic realities confronting the nation and expressed support for the Federal Government’s current position on fuel subsidy.” “The meeting resolved that the reintroduction of fuel subsidy would not serve the long-term interests of national economic development and fiscal sustainability,” the communiqué stated. The monarchs also called for stronger political and economic engagement to ensure that the interests of the South-West were adequately represented and protected within the Nigerian federation. They stressed the need for the region to remain vigilant and strategically engaged in national affairs, particularly on issues affecting its political relevance, economic advancement and developmental aspirations. Beyond regional interests, the Council called for stronger national integration and constructive engagement among traditional institutions across the country’s geopolitical zones. It pledged to strengthen relationships with traditional rulers in Northern Nigeria and other parts of the federation, noting that mutual understanding and cooperation remained essential to peace, unity and national development. “Recognising the importance of national integration, the Council called for stronger collaboration and mutual understanding among all regions of the country.” “The traditional rulers pledged to foster constructive engagement with their counterparts in Northern Nigeria and other parts of the federation in the interest of peace, unity, and national development,” the communiqué stated. The meeting also commended President Tinubu for the establishment of a new military brigade in Oyo State, describing the development as a significant boost to the security architecture of the South-West. The monarchs expressed appreciation to the president for the military formation, noting that it would strengthen security operations and contribute to the protection of lives and property across the region. “The Council expressed profound appreciation to the President for the establishment of the new military brigade in Oyo State,” the communiqué stated. The traditional rulers added that the development would significantly enhance the region’s security architecture and contribute to safeguarding communities against security threats. They also commended the President and the Federal Government for ongoing infrastructure projects and other developmental initiatives across the South-West and the country. According to the Council, the projects had continued to contribute positively to economic activities, improved connectivity and overall national development. “The meeting acknowledged the positive impact of these projects on economic activities, connectivity, and overall national development,” the communiqué added. item.title: 2027: SDP inaugurates 12,000-member campaign council, names Tanko coordinator
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) has inaugurated a 12,000-member Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, with Dr Yunusa Tanko appointed as its National Coordinator. The SDP National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Gombe, who will also serve as chairman of the council, inaugurated the campaign council on Wednesday in Abuja. Gombe charged members of the council to work towards securing electoral victory for the party, stressing that its campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and guided by the provisions of the Constitution, the Electoral Act, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) guidelines and the party’s constitution. He urged members to approach the election with the seriousness it deserved, adding that the party was determined to challenge President Bola Tinubu at the polls. “Let us approach this election with the seriousness it deserves to unseat President Tinubu. “Our campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and firmly rooted in the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the Electoral Act, INEC guidelines and our party constitution. “We must earn the confidence of Nigerians through credible engagement, persuasion, effective organisation and practical policy alternatives. “We must reject violence, intimidation, electoral malpractice and every conduct capable of undermining the integrity of our democracy,” he said. The SDP chairman described Nigeria as being at a critical crossroads, citing insecurity, economic hardship, unemployment, poverty, institutional weaknesses and declining public confidence in governance as some of the challenges confronting the country. According to him, Nigerians are yearning for purposeful leadership, economic opportunities, social justice, security and accountability, as well as a government that prioritises their welfare and dignity. He said the SDP was determined to provide Nigerians with a credible democratic alternative founded on social justice, equity, freedom, inclusive development and good governance. Gombe urged members of the campaign council to take the party’s message to communities across the country, engage citizens respectfully, listen to their concerns and demonstrate through their conduct that the party deserved their confidence. He further charged the council to ensure that the party’s campaign remained peaceful, credible and focused on offering practical solutions to the country’s challenges. The post 2027: SDP inaugurates 12,000-member campaign council, names Tanko coordinator appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Spain: General strike over housing costs before national election
item.description: Millions of Spanish workers shut down businesses and public transportation in a protest on Wednesday over housing costs that the government hopes to leverage before a national election later this month. The walkout — under the slogan “Salaries. Housing. Prices.” — was the first general strike in Spain in 14 years.

item.title: The best early Black Friday deals you can already shop
item.description: The countdown to Black Friday is on, and the first discounts are starting to appear. Although the shopping holiday isn’t officially until November 27th, retailers are already dropping early deals on some of our favorite tech. Of course, with prices rising across the board, a good discount doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting a historically low price. But we’re still seeing worthwhile discounts on a host of tried-and-tested gear, with more expected in the coming weeks. Below, we’ve rounded up the best early Black Friday deals we’ve found so far. Prices could drop further as Black Friday approaches, as is always the case, but these deals are worth considering if you’d rather shop early and beat the holiday rush. We’ll continue to update this guide as more retailers launch their holiday sales, too, so be sure to check back regularly as we get closer to the main event. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before. item.title: Obi prefers ‘anywhere food is ready politics’ – Wike
item.description: Says, Atiku won’t get 25% across South By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC, Mr Peter Obi, prefers “anywhere food is ready politics”. Wike spoke on Tuesday when he met youth stakeholders in the FCT to campaign for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the January presidential election. “Obi is not going anywhere. Don’t deceive yourself. If he likes, let him enter the motorcycle and carry everybody at the back; he is not going anywhere,” the minister said. He mocked Obi’s visits to camps for internally displaced persons (IDPs). ” He goes to IDP camp to do birthdays. When he was governor, did he do that? No. Very soon, they will start going along the trees, buying and chewing corn. “He prefers anywhere Mama Put is ready for politics. He doesn’t want to struggle. Small fight, he ran away from the PDP. He did the same in the Labour Party, and now he is in NDC. But, as for me, I am not afraid of fighting. They have now run away from the PDP, and I am still in the party,” he said. The minister also dismissed the chances of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, the African Democratic Congress ADC presidential candidate. “Atiku won’t get 25 per cent in South South, South East and South West. Where will he get it?” he asked. He urged the youths to do more than vote for Tinubu. “Please, I beg of you, not to just come out to vote, not to just endorse this president here, mobilise all your colleagues, even those who are not part of your association, reach out to them, and get everybody to come out. “I am not a member of the All Progressives Congress. You don’t need to be an APC member or a Peoples Democratic Party PDP member for you to contribute to the development of your country. All you need to do is to work according to the vision of the person who has appointed you. Let’s not put our destiny in the hands of political gamblers who have been gambling for over 22 years,” he said. Wike reminded the youths of the record of earlier administrations on their welfare and that of women in the FCT. “Atiku Abubakar was vice president from 1999 to 2007. Is it not correct? Correct. Was there any establishment of a youth secretariat? No. Was there any establishment of a women’s secretariat? No. From 1976 to 2023, nobody cared,” he added. He said Tinubu changed that within a year of taking office. “Go and make sure there is a youth secretary. Go and make sure there’s a woman secretary,” he quoted the president as directing. He urged the youths to ignore showmanship. “Leave all these rhetorics; leave all this drama. These are cosmetic. Let us face the reality on the ground. That is what matters,” he said. The post Obi prefers ‘anywhere food is ready politics’ – Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Omotunde’s 5 Days in South Korea: Exploring LG’s World of Innovation & Discovering the Best of Korean Culture
item.description: Hello BNers, Omotunde here. From exploring futuristic smart homes and AI-powered manufacturing facilities to tasting Korean street food, discovering Seoul, and experiencing the country’s rich culture, my 5-day South Korea adventure with LG Electronics was unforgettable. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) Some trips leave you with beautiful photographs, others with unforgettable memories, and some leave you with a whole new perspective. My experience in South Korea with LG Electronics was a combination of all three. South Korea had been on my travel wish list for a while, so finally getting the opportunity to visit was exciting in itself. But this was more than just a trip to a new destination. It was an opportunity to explore the world of LG Electronics, understand its journey, experience its innovations firsthand and discover how technology continues to shape the way we live. Over five days, we explored different locations, met incredible people, exchanged ideas, experienced some of Korea’s most exciting innovations and, of course, made time to enjoy the country’s food, culture and lifestyle. From Seoul to Changwon , every day brought something new. Here’s a look at how the experience unfolded. PART ONE: THE LG INNOVATION TOUR Our LG experience began with an introduction to the company’s vision, its Home Appliance Solutions business, and its ambition to become a Smart Life Solution Company. While many of us know LG for its home appliances, televisions, and consumer electronics, the tour offered a much broader understanding of the brand and the thinking behind its innovations. At the LG Twin Towers, we were introduced to different aspects of the company’s business and got to explore some of its products and technologies, including the LG WashTower, InstaView refrigerator, Heat Pump Washer Dryer Combo, SolarDOM, and SKS premium appliances. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) What stood out to me was how much attention is being given to making everyday living smarter, more convenient, and more connected. My experience in South Korea with LG Electronics was a combination of all three. Over five days, we explored different locations, met incredible people, exchanged ideas, experienced some of Korea’s most exciting innovations and, of course, made time to enjoy the country’s food, culture and lifestyle. From Seoul to Changwon , every day brought something new. Here’s a look at how the experience unfolded. PART ONE: THE LG INNOVATION TOUR Our LG experience began with an introduction to the company’s vision, its Home Appliance Solutions business, and its ambition to become a Smart Life Solution Company. While many of us know LG for its home appliances, televisions, and consumer electronics, the tour offered a much broader understanding of the brand and the thinking behind its innovations. At the LG Twin Towers, we were introduced to different aspects of the company’s business and got to explore some of its products and technologies, including the LG WashTower, InstaView refrigerator, Heat Pump Washer Dryer Combo, SolarDOM, and SKS premium appliances. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) What stood out to me was how much attention is being given to making everyday living smarter, more convenient, and more connected. It was interesting to see how products that perform familiar household functions are evolving through technology to offer entirely new experiences. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) It was a great introduction to what would become five days of learning and discovery. Changwon Smart Park: Where AI, Robotics and Manufacturing Meet One of the most insightful experiences of the tour was visiting LG Smart Park in Changwon. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) Before this visit, my idea of a manufacturing facility was largely shaped by traditional production lines and machinery. However, what I encountered at Changwon offered a completely different perspective. From the Heritage Lounge , where we got an introduction to LG’s manufacturing journey, to the Lighthouse Factory experience, there was so much to learn about how the company is integrating artificial intelligence, robotics, data and automation into its manufacturing processes. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) Recognised by the World Economic Forum as a Lighthouse Factory, LG Smart Park demonstrates how advanced technologies can transform manufacturing and improve efficiency. Seeing how robots, intelligent systems and people work together was particularly fascinating. It also got me thinking about the ongoing conversations around artificial intelligence and the future of work. Rather than simply viewing AI as a technology that replaces human effort, I got to see how it can support people, take on repetitive tasks and improve the way complex processes are managed. It was one of those visits that makes you appreciate just how much goes on behind the products we use every day. LG Science Park: A Glimpse Into the Future Our next stop was LG Science Park in Magok, Seoul, one of the company’s major research and development hubs. This was another opportunity to see how LG is thinking about the future of technology and everyday living. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) We explored the LG AI Home experience, ThinQ Real Home, the Innovation Showroom and the D5 flagship experience. The demonstrations offered a glimpse into what connected living could look like, with smart technologies and appliances working together to create a more seamless home experience. Imagine a home where your appliances communicate with one another, respond intelligently to your needs and make everyday routines easier. That was the kind of future these experiences brought to life. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) It was fascinating seeing how research, technology and innovation are being translated into solutions that could eventually become part of our everyday lives. And just when I thought there was already so much to take in, I got to meet CLOiD ! View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) Meeting CLOiD: When the Future Becomes Real Meeting a live robot called CLOiD was definitely one of those surreal moments of the trip. We have seen robots in movies and watched countless videos of artificial intelligence and robotics, but seeing one up close and experiencing it in person is something else entirely. It was fascinating to see how far robotics has come and how these technologies are moving beyond futuristic concepts into real-world applications. Experiences like this make you pause and think about how different our everyday lives could look in the years ahead. From Goldstar to LG: Understanding the Evolution of a Global Brand Another interesting part of the tour was learning more about LG’s history and evolution. The company’s story dates back to 1947, when it began as Lak Hui Chemical. In 1958, Goldstar was established, marking its entry into the electronics industry. The company eventually adopted the LG identity in 1995. Getting to see this journey represented through its history, milestones and innovations gave me a deeper appreciation of how the brand has evolved over the decades. It was particularly interesting learning about some of LG’s early milestones, including its first electric fan in 1960, refrigerator in 1965, air conditioner in 1968 and washing machine in 1969. From those early innovations to the smart appliances and technologies we explored during the tour, it was a remarkable reminder of how far the company has come. It also reinforced something I took away from the experience: innovation is not a one-time achievement. It requires continuous learning, improvement and the willingness to imagine what is possible beyond the present. The LG Flagship Store: Experiencing Innovation in One Space Our visit to the LG Flagship Store was a lovely way to bring different aspects of the tour together. Having spent the preceding days learning about LG’s history, exploring its manufacturing facilities and experiencing its smart home technologies, visiting the flagship store offered another opportunity to interact with the brand’s innovations in one space. One of my favourite experiences there was the Vision Hall. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BellaNaija (@bellanaija) Stepping into the space felt like stepping into another world. The colours, visuals and immersive displays created such a beautiful cinematic experience. It was almost otherworldly, and I found myself completely immersed in the moment. Beyond the visual experience, it made me appreciate how far technology has come and the possibilities that innovation continues to create. It was one of those experiences that was difficult to put into words, so naturally, I had to make a little movie out of it! PART TWO: EXPLORING KOREA Beyond the LG tour, one of t

item.title: Kerrygold Engages Women in Business and Leadership at 25th WIMBIZ Annual Conference
item.description: Kerrygold, the renowned Irish dairy brand from Ornua, strengthened its engagement with consumers at the 25th Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ) Annual Conference, held on November 5 and 6, 2026, at Eko Hotel & Suites, Lagos. The conference, which marked 25 years of WIMBIZ’s commitment to empowering women, brought together business leaders, entrepreneurs, professionals and public sector executives for conversations around leadership, enterprise development and the evolving role of women in business. This year’s edition was themed “Rooted, Rising, Ready: Born in Africa, Built for the World.” As a sponsor of the conference, Kerrygold leveraged the platform to increase brand visibility, deepen consumer engagement and strengthen its relevance among an audience of accomplished and influential women. A key feature of its participation was an exhibition stand where attendees had the opportunity to discover the brand, learn more about its product offerings and sample its products. The activation provided an opportunity for direct interaction with consumers, allowing guests to experience Kerrygold firsthand while creating meaningful brand touchpoints beyond traditional brand visibility. Through these engagements, Kerrygold reinforced its commitment to bringing its quality dairy products closer to consumers and building lasting relationships through relevant experiences. Commenting on the brand’s participation, Titilayo Ijiyokunola, General Manager, Ornua Dairy Products Nigeria Ltd., said: “At Kerrygold, we recognise the important role women play in shaping businesses, industries and communities. Our participation at WIMBIZ provides an opportunity to connect with this community, recognise their contributions and support platforms that champion leadership, enterprise and professional growth.” Kerrygold’s participation at the conference reflects its continued interest in engaging consumers through platforms that bring people together, create opportunities for meaningful interactions and allow more people to experience the quality and distinctive offerings of the brand. About Kerrygold Kerrygold is a globally trusted Irish dairy brand renowned for its quality, rich taste and provenance. Built on generations of dairy knowledge and heritage, Kerrygold is made with the finest milk from grass-fed cows and quality ingredients, with no artificial ingredients. In Nigeria, Kerrygold Milk is manufactured and distributed by Ornua Nigeria, bringing the brand’s distinctive rich, creamy taste and heritage to consumers across the country. The post Kerrygold Engages Women in Business and Leadership at 25th WIMBIZ Annual Conference appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Patrick Stewart Made Anthony Mackie ‘Freak Out’ on Avengers: Doomsday Set
item.description: Patrick Stewart died on Oct. 28, meaning that his performance as Professor Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday will be the last of his long career. Stewart first played the telepathic mutant in Bryan Singer’s X-Men in 2000, leading the superhero team in the fight against Ian McKellen’s Magneto. The two actors had met decades before at the Royal Shakespeare Company, but they became close friends after working together on the X-Men films. The actors reunited for Avengers: Doomsday , and Anthony Mackie said he and his The Falcon and the Winter Soldier co-star Sebastian Stan were so excited about it that they embarrassed themselves.

item.title: ADC to EFCC, INEC: Probe alleged cash, gift distribution by APC officials
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has called on the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to investigate alleged distribution of cash and gifts by All Progressives Congress (APC) officials at political events. The party urged the two agencies to examine the reported incidents and publicly disclose the steps being taken to address any possible violations of electoral and currency laws. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, accused the ruling party of attempting to manufacture support for President Bola Tinubu through financial inducements. The call followed the circulation of a video showing the Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, distributing bundles of cash and APC-branded wrappers to women at a political gathering in Rivers State. The 45-second video, shared on TikTok by Move with Imaan, an account documenting the minister’s activities, showed Sulaiman-Ibrahim handing out bundles of cash and a bale of wrappers bearing the APC logo to women at the gathering. The video also showed her distributing cash in envelopes bearing the images of Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima, with recipients appearing to receive bundles of N1,000 notes. ‘Pattern becoming impossible to ignore’ Reacting to the development, Shaibu alleged that the distribution of money and gifts at political gatherings was an attempt to buy public support amid prevailing economic hardship. “The pattern is becoming impossible to ignore. From reports of luxury vehicles presented to APC women leaders, to cash and cooked food distributed by the President’s son through the City Boy Movement, and now videos circulating of an APC women leader handing out money and fabrics, the ruling party appears to be treating political support as something that can be bought,” he said. The ADC spokesperson described the alleged distributions as particularly insensitive at a time when millions of Nigerians were struggling to afford food, transportation and other basic necessities. He also questioned why ordinary Nigerians had faced sanctions over alleged abuse of the naira while political operatives appeared to be distributing cash at campaign events. “The same authorities that have pursued ordinary Nigerians over alleged abuse of the Naira must explain why apparent cash distribution by political operatives at campaign events should be treated differently,” he said. “The EFCC and INEC must investigate these incidents and take appropriate action wherever electoral or currency laws have been breached.” Shaibu also accused the Tinubu administration of worsening economic hardship, rising insecurity and public debt, arguing that cash and gifts could not erase the difficulties confronting Nigerian households. “After three and a half years of economic hardship, rising insecurity and mounting public debt, the

The ADC spokesperson described the alleged distributions as particularly insensitive at a time when millions of Nigerians were struggling to afford food, transportation and other basic necessities. He also questioned why ordinary Nigerians had faced sanctions over alleged abuse of the naira while political operatives appeared to be distributing cash at campaign events. “The same authorities that have pursued ordinary Nigerians over alleged abuse of the Naira must explain why apparent cash distribution by political operatives at campaign events should be treated differently,” he said. “The EFCC and INEC must investigate these incidents and take appropriate action wherever electoral or currency laws have been breached.” Shaibu also accused the Tinubu administration of worsening economic hardship, rising insecurity and public debt, arguing that cash and gifts could not erase the difficulties confronting Nigerian households. “After three and a half years of economic hardship, rising insecurity and mounting public debt, the APC has little to show Nigerians,” he said. “Its answer is to display cash and gifts at political events, as though a brief handout can erase the daily struggle families face or buy their votes.” He further alleged that the administration had pushed millions of Nigerians deeper into poverty and questioned the scale, terms and utilisation of government borrowing. The ADC spokesperson maintained that political support could not be secured through financial inducements, insisting that Nigerians would determine the outcome of the next election through their votes. “No amount of money can compel Nigerians to endorse a government that has made life harder for them. The people’s votes are not for sale, and no manufactured crowd can substitute for their verdict at the ballot box,” he said. “President Tinubu has failed Nigerians. No cash handout can buy back their trust.” The post ADC to EFCC, INEC: Probe alleged cash, gift distribution by APC officials appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro does not like to be taken apart
item.description: Apple's first touchscreen MacBook got a mixed reception from iFixit's teardown specialists, who praised its easily replaced lid but found fans and USB-C ports buried beneath the logic board. The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display was unveiled at the end of October. It features a tandem OLED screen that stacks two layers of organic light-emitting pixels, eliminating the need for a backlight, and adds touch capability to the MacBook line for the first time. Although the vendor was patted on the back in recent years for improving the repairability of its famously locked-down products, this machine shows Apple still has some way to go. The good? The entire lid comes off relatively easily. Its three-screw hinges closely resemble those on the M6 14-inch MacBook Pro, while streamlined display cable brackets simplify removal. Apple's Repair Assistant tool also handled a full system board swap well. Despite concerns about Touch ID fingerprint authentication, everything went relatively smoothly when iFixit paired a touchscreen from one machine with a logic board from another. On the first boot, Repair Assistant recognized the battery, display, and Touch ID sensor, and touch control needed no separate calibration. The bad? Replacing the panel alone is not possible. When iFixit tried to separate it from the lid, the glass delaminated, cracking the OLED and touch-sensitive layers beneath. That could make for a costlier repair than bargained for. Under the bottom cover, the PROLED has a similar internal layout to the last few models of MacBook Pros, with the fans, board, speakers, and trackpad all in the same places. That means the same annoyances persist. The MagSafe power connector can be removed via two screws and a bracket, yet the USB-C ports can't be extracted the same way because the logic board is in the way. The headphone jack and the fans also require removing the system board first, and the HDMI port and SDXC card reader are soldered to the board itself, as is the storage and memory. Another gripe is that this MacBook's battery pack is hard to remove, though at least it is removable, unlike in many thin-and-light laptops. The tested Pro weighs 1.38 kg or about 3 pounds. For these reasons, the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display earns a 5 out of 10 repairability score from iFixit , but this is actually a one point increase over the score it gave the M5 MacBook Pro. The Apple logo has its own lighting. Older MacBooks with illuminated logos borrowed light from the LCD backlight shining through an apple-shaped window in the lid. This model uses a strip of LEDs along one edge of the logo, passing through a diffuser for an even glow. Because it sits behind the display panel, it would be nearly impossible to repair if it failed, especially if the panel is destroyed during removal. Under a microscope, the PROLED XDR display looks very different from earlier MacBooks: the blue subpixel is significantly larger than the green and red ones. The reason, we're t

That means the same annoyances persist. The MagSafe power connector can be removed via two screws and a bracket, yet the USB-C ports can't be extracted the same way because the logic board is in the way. The headphone jack and the fans also require removing the system board first, and the HDMI port and SDXC card reader are soldered to the board itself, as is the storage and memory. Another gripe is that this MacBook's battery pack is hard to remove, though at least it is removable, unlike in many thin-and-light laptops. The tested Pro weighs 1.38 kg or about 3 pounds. Under a microscope, the PROLED XDR display looks very different from earlier MacBooks: the blue subpixel is significantly larger than the green and red ones. The reason, we're told, is that blue OLED materials wear out faster, so a larger subpixel can emit the same amount of light while putting less strain on the material. ®

item.title: Sharge’s eye-catching MacBook charger is over 25 percent off
item.description: Looking for a MacBook and device charger that’s as stylish as it is capable? Both Amazon and Sharge are selling the Pixel 140W GaN charger for $69.88 and $69.90, respectively, a $24 discount on its usual price. If you’re not in need of that much wattage but like the style, Sharge is also selling the 67W version for $19.90 ($30 off) or the 100W version for $59.90 ($16 off). Sharge Pixel 140 GaN Charger Where to Buy: $90.9 $69.88 at Amazon $90.9 $69.9 at Sharge The Pixel 140 delivers up to 140W of power when using only one of its three USB-C ports, which Sharge says is capable of taking a 16-inch MacBook Pro from a flat battery to 50 percent charge in just 25 minutes. It’s 47 percent smaller than the MacBook’s included charging brick as well, which is great if you’re tight on bag space or travel frequently. The pixel display on the side has configurable brightness and orientation, and displays your current charging wattage. Other deals to consider Halo fans looking for a fun weeknight project can grab Mattel’s Brick Shop Warthog on Amazon for $62.99 ($12 off), which is the lowest price we’ve seen on the brick-ified UNSC replica. The 935-piece set lets you recreate a 1:22 scale model of the iconic land vehicle, and includes a 1:64 scale metal version as well. Windows users with Mac Mini envy might consider the Lenovo Yoga Mini , which is currently discounted to $599.99 ($460 off) at Best Buy as part of the retailer’s early Black Friday promo. The compact desktop PC features an Intel Core Ultra 5 processor, 16GB of LPDDR5X memory, and 512GB of storage; it also has several fun features, including automated lighting around the system and Wi-Fi presence sensing. While modern smartphone camera stabilization has improved dramatically, there are still plenty of situations where a motorized gimbal can help you capture a smoother shot. Fortunately, the DJI Osmo Mobile 8 is currently on sale at Amazon for $89 ($20 off), nearly matching its best price to date. It features 360-degree horizontal panning and over 10 hours of battery life on a single charge.

item.title: Nigeria’s crude oil output drops to 1.51m bpd in October — NUPRC
item.description: Nigeria’s crude oil production declined slightly to 1.51 million barrels per day (bpd) in October 2026, from 1.53 million bpd recorded in September, according to data from the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC). The figure represents a 1.7 per cent month-on-month decline. Despite the drop, Nigeria maintained crude oil production above its Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) quota of 1.5 million bpd for the sixth consecutive month in 2026. OPEC data showed that Nigeria produced 1.5 million bpd in August, 1.50 million bpd in July, 1.55 million bpd in June and 1.53 million bpd in May. When condensates are included, the country’s average daily production stood at 1.68 million barrels in October. NUPRC data also showed that daily production peaked at 1.79 million barrels during the month, while the lowest output was 1.60 million barrels per day. The commission attributed the relatively stable production levels in recent months to improved operational stability, production uptime and crude evacuation efficiency. “The sustained growth recorded in October reflects the continued commitment of operators and industry stakeholders towards improving operational efficiency, maintaining asset integrity, and enhancing production reliability across the Nigerian upstream petroleum sector,” the commission said. A breakdown of daily average crude oil and condensate production by terminals and streams showed that Forcados recorded the highest output at 318,490 barrels per day, followed by Bonny Terminal with 311,020 bpd. Qua Iboe Terminal recorded an average production of 173,970 bpd, while Escravos Oil Terminal posted a daily average of 134,670 bpd. The commission added that Bonga ranked as the fifth-highest producing terminal, recording an average of 106,650 bpd of crude oil and condensate. The post Nigeria’s crude oil output drops to 1.51m bpd in October — NUPRC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reps seek emergency funding for teaching hospitals as health budget falls to 4.2%
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called on the Federal Government to urgently increase funding for federal teaching hospitals, federal medical centres, the National Hospital Abuja and other tertiary health institutions, warning that inadequate resources are undermining specialist healthcare delivery across the country. The lawmakers also urged the government to establish a dedicated infrastructure revitalisation programme, improve the welfare of healthcare workers and ensure timely release of approved funds to the institutions. The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Patrick Umoh during Wednesday’s plenary, in which he drew attention to declining health budget allocations, deteriorating infrastructure, inadequate medical equipment and the continued migration of doctors, nurses and other skilled professionals. Presenting the motion, Umoh said federal tertiary health institutions remained central to specialist medical services, healthcare training and research but were struggling with dilapidated facilities, insufficient bed spaces, unreliable electricity supply and rising operational costs. He said urgent legislative intervention was necessary to strengthen the institutions and ensure that Nigerians had access to quality, affordable and accessible specialist healthcare. The lawmaker also commended the Federal Government for its continued interest in and prioritisation of the health sector. However, he expressed concern that Nigeria’s health sector allocation remained significantly below the 15 per cent commitment made by African governments under the 2001 Abuja Declaration. According to the motion, the proposed federal health budget allocation declined from approximately 5.33 per cent in 2023 to 4.20 per cent in the proposed 2026 budget. Umoh also cited figures indicating that only 30 per cent of the health sector’s 2023 capital appropriation was released, while approximately 15.06 per cent of the 2024 capital allocation was reportedly released and utilised. The motion further stated that only N36 million was reportedly released from the N218 billion appropriated for the Ministry of Health’s 2025 capital expenditure. The lawmaker warned that inadequate funding had contributed to overcrowded hospitals, delays in treatment, poor maintenance of facilities and shortages of essential medical equipment, forcing some patients to seek treatment in private hospitals or abroad. He also linked the growing migration of doctors, consultants and nurses to the declining capacity of public tertiary hospitals to provide specialist services. Umoh said the recently reported Ebola case in Nigeria had further underscored the need to strengthen the country’s tertiary health institutions and their capacity to respond to public health emergencies. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called on the Federal Government to urgently increase funding for federal teaching hospitals, federal medical centres, the National Hospital Abuja and other tertiary health institutions, warning that inadequate resources are undermining specialist healthcare delivery across the country. The lawmakers also urged the government to establish a dedicated infrastructure revitalisation programme, improve the welfare of healthcare workers and ensure timely release of approved funds to the institutions. The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Patrick Umoh during Wednesday’s plenary, in which he drew attention to declining health budget allocations, deteriorating infrastructure, inadequate medical equipment and the continued migration of doctors, nurses and other skilled professionals. Presenting the motion, Umoh said federal tertiary health institutions remained central to specialist medical services, healthcare training and research but were struggling with dilapidated facilities, insufficient bed spaces, unreliable electricity supply and rising operational costs. He said urgent legislative intervention was necessary to strengthen the institutions and ensure that Nigerians had access to quality, affordable and accessible specialist healthcare. The lawmaker also commended the Federal Government for its continued interest in and prioritisation of the health sector. However, he expressed concern that Nigeria’s health sector allocation remained significantly below the 15 per cent commitment made by African governments under the 2001 Abuja Declaration. According to the motion, the proposed federal health budget allocation declined from approximately 5.33 per cent in 2023 to 4.20 per cent in the proposed 2026 budget. Umoh also cited figures indicating that only 30 per cent of the health sector’s 2023 capital appropriation was released, while approximately 15.06 per cent of the 2024 capital allocation was reportedly released and utilised. The motion further stated that only N36 million was reportedly released from the N218 billion appropriated for the Ministry of Health’s 2025 capital expenditure. The lawmaker warned that inadequate funding had contributed to overcrowded hospitals, delays in treatment, poor maintenance of facilities and shortages of essential medical equipment, forcing some patients to seek treatment in private hospitals or abroad. He also linked the growing migration of doctors, consultants and nurses to the declining capacity of public tertiary hospitals to provide specialist services. Umoh said the recently reported Ebola case in Nigeria had further underscored the need to strengthen the country’s tertiary health institutions and their capacity to respond to public health emergencies. Consequently, the House urged the Federal Government to substantially increase allocations to federal teaching hospitals, medical centres, the National Hospital Abuja and other tertiary institutions in the 2027 Supplementary Appropriation Bill and subsequent budgets. It also called for a dedicated tertiary healthcare infrastructure revitalisation programme to rehabilitate existing facilities, expand hospital capacity and provide modern medical equipment. On manpower, the lawmakers urged the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare to conduct a comprehensive assessment of staffing needs across federal tertiary institutions and develop a properly funded recruitment and retention programme. They further called for improved welfare packages, specialist allowances, professional development opportunities and other incentives to discourage healthcare professionals from leaving public hospitals. The House also urged the Federal Ministry of Finance and the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation to ensure the timely and adequate release of approved allocations, particularly capital and overhead funds. Other recommendations included dedicated funding for electricity, water supply, equipment maintenance, medical consumables and other essential operational needs of the institutions. The House unanimously adopted the motion and mandated its Committee on Health Institutions to engage relevant ministries, the Budget Office of the Federation and hospital managements to develop a sustainable funding and revitalisation framework. The committee was also directed to monitor the implementation of the recommendations and report periodically to the House. item.title: Trump wanted little Kei trucks for America, Toyota makes it happen
item.description: The idea that Americans should be offered a greater choice of smaller cars has support from strange bedfellows indeed. After all, who could forget President Trump—usually one to take a maximalist approach to any problem— announcing last year that he wanted the Department of Transportation to make Japan’s diminutive “Kei” cars legal here in the US. Ars’ attempts to get DoT to tell us more about the potential influx of little vehicles have mostly fallen on deaf ears. But this week, there has been movement on the topic, with Toyota announcing that it will bring back the Scion brand with the KEI-01. What’s a Kei car? Here in the US, the preponderance of humongous SUVs is a consequence largely of government policies, specifically corporate average fuel economy standards that made it less profitable to sell smaller, efficient cars. Japan’s Kei cars are what happens if the government instead restricts the size, engine capacity, and power output. Read full article Comments

item.title: Tinubu recycling failed 2023 promises in 2027 manifesto, says ADC
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has accused President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress, APC, of recycling unfulfilled 2023 campaign promises in their newly unveiled 2027 manifesto, challenging the President to account for his record before seeking another mandate. The party said the manifesto reads like the programme of a political party seeking power for the first time, rather than that of a government that has controlled the Federal Government for nearly 12 years and has had more than three years under Tinubu to deliver on its promises. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC cited healthcare coverage, ICT job creation and electricity generation as examples of promises it said the administration had failed to fulfil, questioning why Nigerians should be asked to embrace another set of commitments without an account of the previous ones. “The fundamental question Nigerians must ask is simple: Why is a government campaigning on promises it should already have fulfilled? President Tinubu has been in office since May 2023. The APC has controlled the Federal Government for nearly twelve years. Yet, reading this manifesto, one would think they are only now discovering the problems they were elected to solve,” the ADC said. The party recalled that Tinubu had promised in 2023 to extend health insurance coverage to 40 per cent of Nigerians within two years and create one million ICT jobs within 24 months. It claimed that barely one in ten Nigerians was now covered by health insurance, while government figures indicated that only about 15,000 jobs and opportunity pathways had been recorded, with the health insurance target shifted to 2031. The ADC also questioned the administration’s electricity performance, pointing out that the APC had described 4,500 megawatts of power generation as a crisis in 2023, only for its new manifesto to acknowledge average generation of 4,022 megawatts. “How does a government campaign to solve a crisis it has made remarkably worse?” the party queried. The opposition party further faulted Tinubu’s promise to introduce a programme for his first 100 days after re-election, arguing that the president already had the executive powers to implement the proposed measures without waiting for another electoral victory. “Most astonishingly, President Tinubu now promises a programme for his first 100 days after re-election, including measures he already possesses the executive powers to implement right now. What exactly is stopping him from acting today? What stopped him from acting in 2023 when he came into office?” the ADC asked. What exactly is stopping him from acting today? What stopped him from acting in 2023 when he came into office?” the ADC asked. In the economy, the party accused the President of seeking another mandate without addressing the hardship confronting millions of households, claiming that poverty had risen to 63 per cent and the N70,000 minimum wage had lost more than a quarter of its purchasing power. “Yet, rather than account for the hardship he has inflicted on Nigerians and his long catalogue of failures across the economy and security sectors, the president and his party have the temerity to present another colourful brochure full of the same undelivered promises,” the statement said. The ADC insisted that campaign promises could no longer substitute for an assessment of the administration’s performance. “A manifesto is a promise of what a party will do. A record is evidence of what it has done. After eleven years, the APC cannot keep presenting promises as a substitute for performance,” it declared. It challenged Tinubu to publish a comprehensive account of his 2023 commitments, detailing what he had delivered, what remained unfulfilled and why the deadlines were missed, rather than shifting targets and repackaging old promises. The party said the 2027 election would be a referendum on Tinubu’s performance since assuming office, not an opportunity for him to present his presidency as though it were just beginning. “The President must understand that 2027 is first a referendum on his abysmal record since 2023, not an opportunity to pretend that his presidency is just about to begin. Nigeria needs a change of government, not another change of slogans,” the ADC declared. The post Tinubu recycling failed 2023 promises in 2027 manifesto, says ADC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Manchester United ‘Reach Verbal Agreement’ With Ex-Chelsea Coach Pochettino To Replace Carrick
item.description: Manchester United have reportedly reached a “verbal agreement in principle” with Argentine Mauricio Pochettino to replace embattled Michael Carrick as their manager in a bid to revive the fortunes of the struggling English giants. Carrick’s position at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. He remains in post, but it is believed Carrick’s future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday. Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United States head coach Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. It was only three months ago, however, that Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup. US Soccer would be due compensation should he move to Manchester, with the 54-year-old understood to have a $10 million (£7.5 million) release clause. But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have “reached a verbal agreement in principle” with Pochettino, linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach. Turbulent Reign Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training ground on Wednesday, but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. Manchester United’s English head coach Michael Carrick reacts on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge in London on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) The 45-year-old had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. But United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It appeared former United and England midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed Aston Villa by two goals on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But a change now appears likely, with former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann also linked with the United job. In this file photo, ex-Tottenham Hotspur’s Italian head coach Antonio Conte arrives for the English Premier League football match between Fulham and Tottenham Hotspur at Craven Cottage in London on January 23, 2023. item.content:encoded: Manchester United have reportedly reached a “verbal agreement in principle” with Argentine Mauricio Pochettino to replace embattled Michael Carrick as their manager in a bid to revive the fortunes of the struggling English giants. Carrick’s position at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. He remains in post, but it is believed Carrick’s future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday. Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United States head coach Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. It was only three months ago, however, that Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup. US Soccer would be due compensation should he move to Manchester, with the 54-year-old understood to have a $10 million (£7.5 million) release clause. But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have “reached a verbal agreement in principle” with Pochettino, linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach. Turbulent Reign Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training ground on Wednesday, but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. Manchester United’s English head coach Michael Carrick reacts on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge in London on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) The 45-year-old had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. But United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It appeared former United and England midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed Aston Villa by two goals on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But a change now appears likely, with former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann also linked with the United job. In this file photo, ex-Tottenham Hotspur’s Italian head coach Antonio Conte arrives for the English Premier League football match between Fulham and Tottenham Hotspur at Craven Cottage in London on January 23, 2023. (Photo by ADRIAN DENNIS / AFP) . United have the rest of the two-week international break to resolve their managerial situation before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22. Carrick has presided over United’s slide to 18th place — their lowest position 10 games into a top-flight season since 1986/87 when they were 20th. He was hired on a permanent basis in the close season after leading United to a third-place finish in the Premier League during his spell as interim boss. Carrick had won plaudits for steadying the ship after Ruben Amorim’s volatile reign ended in the sack in January. But, hampered by the club’s underwhelming recruitment in the transfer window, Carrick’s team have endured a steep decline this term. United, who have not won the title since Alex Ferguson’s final season as boss in 2012/13, only signed midfielders Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in the summer transfer window despite the glaring need for new forwards. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline among his squad, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager’s tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. He also axed Lisandro Martinez after the United defender criticised the club’s hierarchy for their lack of top-quality signings. United fans have remained largely supportive of Carrick, focusing their anger on the majority owners, the Glazer family, Ratcliffe and the under-achieving players. item.title: Soludo celebrates Anambra-born U-17 Golden Ball winner, Umejiaku
item.description: By Steve Oko Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, has celebrated Oluebube Umejiaku, the Anambra-born midfielder who emerged the Most Valuable Player at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Umejiaku won the prestigious Golden Ball award after inspiring Nigeria’s Flamingos to a historic 2-1 victory over Japan in the final played on November 7. The talented midfielder also scored Nigeria’s decisive second goal, sealing the victory and earning the Player of the Match award in the final. The triumph marked the first time an African women’s national team had won a FIFA World Cup title at any level. Soludo, through his Chief Press Secretary, Christian Aburime, described Umejiaku’s performance at the tournament as superlative. In recognition of her achievement, the Chairman of the Anambra State Football Association, General Chikelue Iloenyosi, travelled to Abuja on November 9 to receive and celebrate the young football star on behalf of the state government. Iloenyosi commended Soludo for his commitment to sports development and efforts to identify and nurture sporting talents across the state. He said Umejiaku’s emergence on the global stage underscored the importance of grassroots sports development and sustained investment in young talents. The Golden Ball winner’s achievement has also been described as a major source of inspiration to aspiring female footballers in Anambra State and the South-East. From her early football development to becoming the standout player at a global tournament, Umejiaku’s rise represents a significant milestone for women’s football in the state. Her performance in Morocco has further highlighted Nigeria’s potential in women’s youth football and placed her among the emerging talents attracting attention on the global stage. The post Soludo celebrates Anambra-born U-17 Golden Ball winner, Umejiaku appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Exclusive: EU's Kallas says US 'can't negotiate on our behalf' on lifting Russia sanctions
item.description: In an exclusive interview with FRANCE 24, the EU's top diplomat Kaja Kallas discusses the war in Ukraine, the situation in the Middle East and a possible change in US President Donald Trump's foreign policy following the US midterm elections. The former Estonian prime minister, who is now the European Union's High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, also reaffirms the EU's position as a major player on the global geopolitical stage.

item.title: 2027: IGP Disu warns police against partisan politics
item.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has warned police officers against partisan political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that the Nigeria Police Force must remain neutral and loyal to the Constitution. Disu gave the warning on Wednesday while addressing senior police officers, including Deputy Inspectors-General of Police, zonal Assistant Inspectors-General and Commissioners of Police, at the monthly meeting of the Goodluck Ebele Peacekeeping Centre. He said the police had a responsibility to provide a safe and secure environment for all electoral participants, irrespective of their political affiliations. The IGP warned that he would not tolerate any officer using the authority of the police to advance the interests of political parties, candidates or their sponsors. He said officers found colluding with political actors, facilitating thuggery, compromising the electoral process or interfering with voters’ rights would face disciplinary action in accordance with the law. “As we approach another important electoral period, I wish to emphasise that it is our responsibility to guarantee a safe and secure environment for all electoral participants, irrespective of their political affiliation. “Every candidate, political party, supporter and eligible voter is entitled to equal protection under the law,” he said. Disu directed Commissioners of Police to commence comprehensive preparations for election security in their respective commands. He ordered the immediate cancellation of leave for officers and personnel assigned to election security duties, adding that Commissioners of Police and other senior officers must remain in their respective commands until the conclusion of the electoral process. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By: Kingsley Omonobi The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has warned police officers against partisan political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that the Nigeria Police Force must remain neutral and loyal to the Constitution. Disu gave the warning on Wednesday while addressing senior police officers, including Deputy Inspectors-General of Police, zonal Assistant Inspectors-General and Commissioners of Police, at the monthly meeting of the Goodluck Ebele Peacekeeping Centre. He said the police had a responsibility to provide a safe and secure environment for all electoral participants, irrespective of their political affiliations. The IGP warned that he would not tolerate any officer using the authority of the police to advance the interests of political parties, candidates or their sponsors. He said officers found colluding with political actors, facilitating thuggery, compromising the electoral process or interfering with voters’ rights would face disciplinary action in accordance with the law. “As we approach another important electoral period, I wish to emphasise that it is our responsibility to guarantee a safe and secure environment for all electoral participants, irrespective of their political affiliation. “Every candidate, political party, supporter and eligible voter is entitled to equal protection under the law,” he said. Disu directed Commissioners of Police to commence comprehensive preparations for election security in their respective commands. He ordered the immediate cancellation of leave for officers and personnel assigned to election security duties, adding that Commissioners of Police and other senior officers must remain in their respective commands until the conclusion of the electoral process. He said any travel outside their commands would require express approval from Force Headquarters. The IGP also directed commands to verify their election security equipment, communication systems, operational vehicles and protective gear and report their readiness by the end of the week. He instructed Commissioners of Police to establish direct coordination with the Independent National Electoral Commission, military, Department of State Services and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps in their respective states. According to him, the police remain the lead agency for election security and must demonstrate effective coordination with other security agencies. He further directed every command to submit daily situation reports to Force Headquarters throughout the electoral period, with the Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations coordinating the reports and briefing him every morning. Disu said personnel must be adequately trained, supervised and equipped to discharge their responsibilities professionally, noting that the Force had embarked on election security training initiatives, including a recent nationwide exercise facilitated by the Nigeria Police Trust Fund. “The Nigeria Police Force is not a tool for any politician, any party or any interest. If you allow yourself to be used, you will face the consequences alone,” he warned. On security operations, the IGP disclosed that police personnel had arrested 218 suspects linked to banditry and terrorism, 85 suspected armed robbers, 129 suspects for murder and culpable homicide, 59 suspected kidnappers and 120 suspected cultists since the last conference. He added that the police had rescued 95 kidnap victims, recovered 306 assorted firearms, 630 rounds of ammunition of various calibres and 116 stolen vehicles. Despite the operational gains, Disu acknowledged that bandit attacks were continuing in some parts of the country, with affected communities facing threats to their safety and livelihoods. He consequently directed Commissioners of Police in affected states to submit updated threat assessments and operational requirements to Force Headquarters within 72 hours. He also ordered the intensification of intelligence-led operations and directed every command to maintain a standing operational plan for high-risk areas. The IGP called for stronger community intelligence, urging police commands to engage traditional rulers, village heads, hunters’ associations and local vigilante groups in affected areas. He also directed the Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations to coordinate the immediate deployment of additional personnel, operational vehicles and air support to the worst-affected areas in consultation with the relevant commands. On police accountability, Disu warned against corruption, extortion, abuse of authority, unlawful use of force and other forms of misconduct. He directed every command to establish accessible and publicised complaints response mechanisms, adding that allegations of police misconduct must be documented, investigated and resolved within specified timelines. He also urged senior officers to maintain regular and transparent engagements with journalists, particularly during the electoral period, when misinformation and fake news could undermine public confidence. The IGP further directed Commissioners of Police to pay attention to the physical and psychological welfare of their personnel, including providing support systems for officers facing operational pressures. He said a welfare audit would be conducted across commands to identify outstanding entitlements, accommodation gaps and other pressing needs, directing that the findings be submitted to his office within 30 days. Disu also commended officers and men whose courage and professionalism had contributed to the achievements recorded by the Force. He paid tribute to police personnel who had lost their lives in the line of duty since the last conference, describing their sacrifices as fundamental to the Force’s operational successes. The IGP disclosed that he had directed the immediate clearance of outstanding death benefits and entitlements owed to families of fallen officers. He also instructed Commissioners of Police to personally verify the status of pending cases involving the families of deceased personnel. While appreciating President Bola Tinubu for his continued support for the police, Disu urged senior officers to return to their commands with renewed determination, stronger supervision and commitment to measurable results. He said the police must ensure that every polling unit opened, every eligible voter was able to cast a ballot and every community facing security threats received adequate protection. He added that every police officer must discharge his or her responsibilities with honour, professionalism and respect for the law. item.title: How years of research built Grand Theft Auto VI’s obsessively detailed world
item.description: The developers behind its virtual Florida share how they built their most ambitious world so far • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here In 2015, a group of Grand Theft Auto developers from Rockstar North took their first trips to Miami to do field research for the next game in the phenomenally popular crime series. “Before you’re doing hyper-organised research trips, you’re immersing yourself in the place and its history, the vibe of it,” Rob Nelson, one of the lead developers on GTA VI, tells me. “[You see] the physical places you want to move characters through, the experiences you want them to have, and the juxtaposition between the extremes of society that are in Miami.” I wondered: did people ever recognise them on any of their research trips? Did locals know what they were doing? This is the biggest game in the world, after all; I imagine it would be difficult to go entirely undercover. “We’re always semi-undercover,” he says. “But if you have a bunch of dorks going through a terrifying neighbourhood, you do stick out a bit.” Continue reading...

item.title: My Grandma Got Me Through the Water Temple. She Would’ve Loved the Ocarina of Time Remake
item.description: For a while it was the NES . I’d shoot ducks until I got bored, and I hated Mario because it was too hard. What I really remember fondly was watching Mémère play The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past after she upgraded to the SNES. She’d tell me who she was fighting and why, and following along felt like having one of my favorite people read me a book. When it was my turn to play, I’d just charge up Link’s sword and mow every blade of grass I could find. Then I’d go looking for chickens. Then I’d ask what she had for snacks. She always had good snacks for me.

item.title: Hubble Space Telescope reveals glittering stars with mysterious origins | Space photo of the day for Nov. 11, 2026
item.description: null The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a breathtaking view of thousands of stars glittering like cosmic jewels in a dazzling display of blue, gold and orange. But this spectacular scene is far more than just a pretty picture. Some of these stars are almost as old as the universe itself and could hold clues to how our Milky Way formed. M30 is a globular star cluster located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth. (Image credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Libralato, G. Piotto, A. Sarajedini) What is it? The exquisite image released by ESA on Nov. 5 shows Messier 30 (M30), a densely packed collection of stars located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus. M30 is a globular cluster, a roughly spherical collection of tens of thousands to millions of stars held together by gravity . Our Milky Way is home to at least 150 of these ancient stellar gatherings, some of which are estimated to be between 11.5 billion and 13.5 billion years old. For comparison, the universe itself is approximately 13.8 billion years old! Why is it amazing Besides looking like a vast cosmic treasure trove glittering across the universe, M30 also has a fascinating story to tell. Globular clusters are essentially cosmic time capsules. Their ancient stars preserve chemical clues about the conditions that existed when they formed, helping astronomers piece together the Milky Way's early history. Astronomers have also discovered that M30, along with several other globular clusters, traverses the Milky Way in the opposite direction to the galaxy's rotation. This unusual motion raises the intriguing possibility that M30 may not have formed in our galaxy at all. It could have simply been captured by the Milky Way billions of years ago.

item.title: Ocarina of Time is even better if you use a smartphone app
item.description: Hey there, buddy. I never liked hunting for Golden Skulltulas in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . The game has 100 of them tucked all over Hyrule, and even over my many hours with the N64 classic growing up, I can't remember ever actually finding all of them, or even wanting to. Jumping into the Ocarina of Time remake , I expected to ignore the Golden Skulltulas once again. But while poking around Nintendo's Zelda Notes companion app, I discovered that its maps are a huge help to tracking down all of the elusive golden spiders - and pretty much every other collectible in the game - and now I find myself constantly opening up the app to make sure I haven't … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
item.description: A graphic representing Google’s AlphaGenome Atlas. | Image: Google Researchers at Google DeepMind have unveiled a new AI model designed to unravel how changes in our DNA affect different cells, giving scientists a more detailed view of a notoriously difficult problem that could hold important clues to the causes of disease - and point the way to new treatments. AlphaGenome 2 is the successor to DeepMind's genome-predicting AI model AlphaGenome, which was released last year . While nearly every cell in the human body carries the same DNA, different types of cells - from heart muscle cells and skin cells to immune cells fighting an infection - switch different genes on and off, and those patterns can change d … Read the full story at The Verge.
